jobs.title: MEP & Structural Sourcing, Director
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Supply Chain Team

Fluidstack builds gigawatt-scale AI data centers with a modular approach that compresses schedules the industry treats as fixed. The Supply Chain team keeps that speed real by getting the longest-lead equipment bought, built, and delivered before the schedule needs it.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Supply gigawatt-scale compute. Qualify and dual-source every critical equipment category, with lead-time and capacity thresholds tied directly to the forward build pipeline.

  • Make supply chain the reason we build faster than anyone. Our modular build lives or dies on supply chain. Keep procurement permanently off the critical path so schedule compression stays our advantage, not our constraint.

  • Build the most accurate supply chain prediction modelling that exists. Use the frontier of AI to forecast lead times, demand, and disruption with a precision the industry has never had.

Role Scope

  • Lead MEP and structural sourcing. Own the electrical, mechanical, and structural steel categories end to end: switchgear, transformers, UPS, generators, busway, chillers, CDUs, pumps, piping packages, and steel.

  • Build and run the team. Hire, develop, and hold accountable the sourcing managers for each category, and set the category strategies they execute.

  • Lock in capacity years ahead. Negotiate capacity reservations and multi-year supply agreements with OEMs, converting reservations to orders as the pipeline firms.

  • Dual-source the critical path. Qualify second sources across equipment classes whose products are not interchangeable, and manage the design implications with engineering.

  • Keep procurement off the critical path. Track factory slots and production milestones supplier by supplier, and escalate before a slipped delivery becomes a slipped data hall.

  • Partner with engineering and manufacturing. Freeze equipment specs early enough to buy at the lead times the market gives, and feed supplier reality back into design decisions.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've led sourcing for major electrical and mechanical equipment (switchgear, transformers, UPS, generation, chillers, CDUs) on large construction or data center programs.

  • You've managed a team of category managers or buyers and can show the results they delivered under you.

  • You've reserved factory capacity ahead of firm designs and managed the commercial risk that creates.

  • You've negotiated multi-year committed-volume agreements with OEMs and held them to price, lead time, and capacity.

  • You know the current lead-time reality of the electrical and mechanical markets by product class, not by rumor.

  • You've expedited equipment through a factory by knowing whom to call and what to trade.

  • You read specifications and drawings well enough to challenge a spec or a price with substance.

  • Bonus: Structural steel and modular skid packages. MV/HV equipment. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling. OFCI programs. Factory witness testing.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.


Applicant Privacy Notice
AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Facility Controls Team

The Facility Controls team builds the control systems behind Fluidstack's data centers: real-time load control, MEP and behind-the-meter integration, automated commissioning, and autonomous deployment.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Deliver the controls behind gigawatt-scale data centers this decade.

  • Own real-time load control and MEP and behind-the-meter integration.

  • Automate Level 4 and Level 5 commissioning.

  • Drive autonomous, robotic deployment.

Role Scope

  • Own the control and data contract between our facility energy controller and third-party power plant controllers. Define the objects, fields, units, update rates and staleness behavior that cross the boundary in each direction.

  • Define the sequences of operation our controller executes. Normal operation, generation shortfall, source transitions, blackstart and emergency shed, along with the degradation behavior for each.

  • Specify the point maps, interlocks and constraint classes that vendors build against. Then hold them to it through factory and site acceptance.

  • Translate between electrical and software. Turn electrical and generation constraints into requirements our software team can build, and turn software and data constraints back into terms a plant vendor and an engineer of record will accept.

  • Prove the interface in simulation before energization. Every constraint class and every mode transition, then carry that work into automated commissioning

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You have worked in the protocols that move data between machines and between systems (MQTT, OPC UA, REST APIs) and you can say why you would pick one over another for a given job rather than reaching for whichever one you used last.

  • You write and read code in at least one language well enough to prototype an integration, test a point map against a live device, and review what the software team ships. Python or Go preferred.

  • You read a one-line and a panel schedule and can say what the protection, the breakers and the sources will actually do under a fault.

  • You have designed a data contract between two systems: the objects, the fields, the units, the update rates, and what a consumer does when a value goes stale. You held both sides to it.

  • You have written the control narrative for a system where two controllers had to agree, and you owned what happened when they disagreed.

  • You sit between the controls world and the software world and you are fluent in both. You have taken a control requirement from an electrical engineer and turned it into something a software team could actually build, and you have pushed back on a software design because it would not survive the field.

  • You have pushed back on a vendor's scope, or on your own company's assumption, with a number rather than an opinion.

  • Bonus: Microgrid and behind-the-meter control (grid-forming BESS, PV plant controllers, turbine and genset dispatch). Utility and industrial protocols (DNP3, IEC 61850 GOOSE, IEC 60870-5-104, Modbus TCP). Schema-driven contracts (OpenAPI, JSON Schema). Automated Level 4 and Level 5 commissioning.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Facility Controls Team

The Facility Controls team builds the control systems behind Fluidstack's data centers: real-time load control, MEP and behind-the-meter integration, automated commissioning, and autonomous deployment.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Deliver the controls behind gigawatt-scale data centers this decade.

  • Own real-time load control and MEP and behind-the-meter integration.

  • Automate Level 4 and Level 5 commissioning.

  • Drive autonomous, robotic deployment.

Role Scope

  • Build and own the facility side of the energy control contract. The production services that carry it: the protocol layer, the gateway service, and the API third-party plant controllers poll against.

  • Design and evolve the messaging and state layer. It computes the facility's load intent from live telemetry and publishes it every second with a forecast ahead of it.

  • Own the data contracts and engineering standards other teams build against. Keep them from drifting as the platform reaches new sites and new counterparties.

  • Build the constraint execution path. It answers an incoming request with what the facility can actually achieve and by when, inside deadlines measured in seconds.

  • Build the observability that proves conformance in production. Per-stage latency, staleness and watchdog health, so a missed budget is visible before it becomes an incident.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You have worked with high-throughput messaging systems (NATS, Kafka, or equivalent) at real scale and you know where the failure modes are before they surface in production.

  • You have designed time-series data models in ClickHouse, TimescaleDB, or a comparable system and you understand the tradeoffs between write throughput, query performance, and schema evolution.

  • You have instrumented production services with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, or equivalent) and you treat metrics and alerting as part of shipping, not something you add after the fact.

  • You have built and owned production services that other teams depend on, and you do not ship code you would not want to be paged for at 3am.

  • You design before you build. You can name the patterns you reach for and why, explain the alternatives you rejected, and point to a system you deliberately refactored because the original design stopped fitting the problem.

  • You draw boundaries on purpose: interfaces, modules and failure domains, so a dependency going down degrades your service instead of taking it with it. The tests you write are the ones that catch the failures you actually fear.

  • You have worked across the full signal chain from device to database, and you treat data integrity as non-negotiable. You work backwards from device-level constraints to build pipelines that are correct by design rather than merely functional, and you handle a stale value differently from a wrong one because both have burned you.

  • You move toward a broken pipeline in production the same way you would move toward any other hard problem: with urgency and without drama.

  • Bonus: Our stack (Go, NATS, Redis). Industrial and utility protocols (DNP3, Modbus TCP, OPC UA). Kubernetes and ArgoCD for production service deployment. Real-time control and dispatch systems (SCADA, EMS, power plant controllers). Real-time dashboarding (Grafana or equivalent).

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

AI Screening Notice

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Construction Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Put gigawatts in the ground, faster than anyone has. We're delivering one of the largest data center buildouts of its kind, with many sites running at once. Traditional construction management breaks at this scale, so we're building the model that replaces it.

  • Throw out traditional construction and invent how gigawatts get built. Tons of tools, layers of process, and administrative drag don't get you there. You'll strip all of that out and win by solving the real problem and beating the goal, not by managing toward it.

  • Productize the data center so we can build it a thousand times. You'll turn one-off construction into a repeatable, modular build, where the hundredth site goes up faster and cleaner than the first. That repeatability is the only way to reach the scale we're targeting.

Role Scope

  • Own day-to-day site execution for greenfield and brownfield GPU data center builds, orchestrating general contractors, trades, and vendors to deliver safe, on-schedule, on-budget facilities at extreme power and cooling density.

  • Build, maintain, and execute integrated schedules (Primavera P6, MS Project) across design, procurement, construction, and commissioning.

  • Enforce the safety program and drive a zero-incident culture across all subcontractors.

  • Coordinate CSA and MEP trades, resolving field conflicts in real time, and verify QA/QC, submittals, RFI, and change-order processes.

  • Track and report daily progress, spend, earned value, and resource loading, and issue recovery plans when needed.

  • Lead scopes of work for critical-path trades and packages, and manage construction contracts from award through close-out.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've managed hyperscale, semiconductor, or mission-critical construction projects.

  • You know CSA and MEP construction phases, procurement workflows, and cost controls deeply.

  • You build and drive integrated schedules in Primavera P6 or MS Project.

  • You enforce safety hard and hold subcontractors to it.

  • You coordinate across Design, Procurement, Commissioning, and Operations and keep handoffs clean.

  • You'll travel 80-100% to active sites. This role runs from the field, not from a desk.

  • Bonus: Construction management qualification. Liquid cooling or high-density power builds. Multi-site international delivery.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.


Applicant Privacy Notice
AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Data Center Operations Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Operate at the scale of a nation, not a building. Accelerating toward 10s to 100s of GWs by the end of the decade, more than the entire electricity consumption of many countries. You won't just run a data center; you'll run infrastructure the size of a G7.

  • Fly the plane while it's being built. Running flawless operations inside a live construction zone, adapting in real time and turning the pace of build-out into our advantage. You will redefine operational excellence.

  • Write the playbook, don't inherit it. Most operators step into someone else's system. Here you build one, leaving your fingerprints on how the whole company runs. As we scale 100x, you'll set the standards, shape the operating model, and grow the team by the thousands.

Role Scope

  • Own end-to-end logistics and asset lifecycle for a hyperscale data center site: receiving, shipping, asset tracking, and vendor coordination.

  • Maintain asset tracking from receipt through decommissioning, including tagging, labeling, and data entry in asset management systems.

  • Manage receiving and shipping: verify quantities, inspect for damage, and update tracking systems in real time.

  • Run cycle audits and physical inventory counts to hold 99%+ accuracy, and resolve shortages before they block build, repair, or deployment.

  • Fulfill parts requests from technicians and engineers fast, and keep staging areas organized for deployment, break-fix, and project material.

  • Process RMAs, warranty claims, and replacements with vendors, coordinate security escorts, and report on inventory performance, turns, and obsolescence.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've owned logistics and asset management on-site in a data center, warehouse, or high-volume hardware environment.

  • You keep inventory accurate to a high bar (99%+) through disciplined cycle counts and real-time tracking.

  • You move material fast under operational pressure, so techs and engineers are never waiting on parts.

  • You manage vendors, RMAs, and inbound and outbound logistics end to end.

  • You build and report metrics (turns, obsolescence, accuracy) and improve the process from them.

  • Bonus: Asset management systems and barcode/RFID tracking. Data center hardware (servers, networking, GPUs). High-growth or hyperscale site operations.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

    • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

      Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Infrastructure Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Design the physical layer AGI is trained on. ISP/OSP cable plants carry hundreds of thousands of fiber terminations per building, rail-optimized for the densest GPU fabrics ever built, at 800G today and 1.6T next.

  • One design, every site. Turn the cable plant from a bespoke months-long exercise into a stamped reference architecture deployed across 10s to 100s of GWs of capacity, validated once and built everywhere.

  • Design for silicon that doesn't exist yet. Every GPU generation rewrites the density, optics, and pathway math, but the plant you spec must survive three of them.

Role Scope

  • Own the end-to-end physical implementation of the data center network: fiber plant architecture, transceiver planning, and structured cabling integration for hyperscale sites.

  • Collaborate with CSA, MEP, and construction teams on power, cooling, space, pathways, cabinets, and racks, and develop, read, and interpret construction drawings in Bluebeam, ACC, and Procore.

  • Break down DCN logical port maps (TOR, spine, super-spine, DCI) into physical cross-connect and patching schedules, and automate port-to-fiber mapping at 100K+ ports per site.

  • Define cassette types (MTP/MPO Base-8/12/16), trunk counts, and structured cabling hierarchy, and model fiber utilization and overbuild for two to three hardware generations.

  • Select optics (400G/800G DR4, FR4, LR4, SR8, coherent DCI) by reach and loss budget, validate interoperability across vendors and generations, and maintain loss-budget and margin models for every link type.

  • Own the ICT Basis of Design, SOPs, and Division 26/27/28/33 master specifications, and integrate with DCIM (NetBox, custom tools) to track strands, ports, and patching.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've designed hyperscale or cloud-provider data center networks (1000+ racks, 100K+ fiber strands).

  • You're expert in structured cabling systems (Corning, Panduit, CommScope) and MPO/MTP ecosystems.

  • You know optical standards (IEEE 802.3, OIF) and transceiver technologies (400G/800G DR4, FR4, LR4, SR8) deeply.

  • You command fiber loss budgets, dispersion, and testing methodologies (OTDR, insertion loss, polarity verification).

  • You integrate designs into DCIM tools (NetBox, Remedy, or custom hyperscaler equivalents).

  • Bonus: RCDD certification. Coherent DCI. Multi-generation optics roadmapping.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.


Applicant Privacy Notice
AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

  • Get power online in months, not years. Most of the clock runs before the lease is ever signed. You'll optimize the pre-signature work, site diligence, permitting, and development, so a site goes from signed lease to live power in under six months.

  • Acquire 10s to 100s of GWs behind the meter. Reaching that scale means generating on-site instead of waiting on grid interconnection. You'll secure the land and behind-the-meter solar generation to get there.

 
 
 

The Development Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Find enough land to deploy multiple gigawatts a week. By 2030 we need to bring on multiple gigawatts of new capacity every week, which means securing sites at a pace and scale no one in the industry has operated at. You'll own finding and locking that land ahead of the build.

  • Get power online in months, not years. Most of the clock runs before the lease is ever signed. You'll optimize the pre-signature work, site diligence, permitting, and development, so a site goes from signed lease to live power in under six months.

  • Acquire 10s to 100s of GWs behind the meter. Reaching that scale means generating on-site instead of waiting on grid interconnection. You'll secure the land and behind-the-meter solar generation to get there.

 
 

Role Scope

  • Own the program management operating rhythm across a multi-GW portfolio of third-party leased and powered shell data center sites, from LOI through construction handoff to operations.

  • Architect and maintain the stage-gate framework that tracks each site from site negotiation through utility lock, lease execution, and BoP construction, ensuring every milestone is visible and every dependency is owned.

  • Build and run the tooling, trackers, and data pipelines that give leadership real-time visibility into schedule, cost, risk, and design changes across 20+ concurrent projects and multiple campuses.

  • Coordinate directly with third-party developers, internal construction, utilities, legal, and finance to surface blockers early and keep deal-to-power timelines under six months.

  • Hand off signed sites to delivery and operations teams with complete documentation, no dropped terms, and no surprises after mobilization.

 
 

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would..

  • You've personally built and run the program management infrastructure for a large, concurrent portfolio of capital projects where the stakes were real and the margin for error was small.

  • You've designed stage-gate or milestone frameworks from scratch and enforced them across teams that didn't report to you.

  • You track 20+ workstreams without losing detail, and the people around you rely on your read of the schedule before they rely on their own.

  • You've coordinated across legal, finance, construction, and external counterparties on deals or projects where the dependencies were messy and the timeline was fixed.

  • You write and speak with enough precision that a senior stakeholder can make a decision off your update without needing a follow-up.

  • Deal discipline, documentation, and process hygiene are habits you hold even when the pace is high and the pressure is to move fast.

  • Bonus: Data center development, powered shell, or build-to-suit project experience. Utility coordination and power delivery timelines. Construction program management at campus scale. Familiarity with BoP scope and construction handoff processes.

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

    • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Supply Chain Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Supply compute at a scale of 10s to 100s of GWs, the largest build out of compute in history. Qualify and dual-source across every critical equipment category, with lead-time and capacity thresholds tied directly to the forward build pipeline.

  • Make supply chain the reason we build faster than anyone. Our modular build redefines speed in this industry, and it lives or dies on supply chain. Keep procurement permanently off the critical path so schedule compression stays our advantage, not our constraint.

  • Build the most accurate supply chain prediction modelling that exists. Use the frontier of AI to forecast lead times, demand, and disruption with a precision the industry has never had, and turn that foresight into a structural edge.

     

Role Scope

  • Own the end-to-end strategy for sourcing, onboarding, and sustaining the contractor workforce and site services that keep Fluidstack's sites running across multiple states.

  • Build and manage a multi-tier supplier network for contract labor: low-voltage electricians, CDU install and maintenance techs, facilities ops, security integrators and guard services, structured cabling crews, and general site trades.

  • Develop preferred-supplier lists and MSA/SOW frameworks with pre-negotiated rate cards and qualification standards for rapid mobilization at new sites.

  • Manage union-jurisdiction awareness (IBEW, NECA) and compliance with prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon, and local labor agreements.

  • Source and negotiate workforce support services (crew housing, catering, transportation, PPE) with volume agreements that scale as site headcount moves through project phases.

  • Partner with Recruiting on contract-to-hire pipelines, and build local workforce-development programs (community colleges, apprenticeships, DOL Registered Apprenticeship) that grow trades capacity where Fluidstack operates.

     

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've sourced and managed contract labor and trades at scale for construction, data center, or industrial operations across multiple sites.

  • You know how to mobilize a skilled workforce fast: rate cards, MSA/SOW frameworks, and qualification standards that travel to new sites.

  • You understand union jurisdictions and labor compliance (prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon) well enough to keep a multi-state buildout clean.

  • You've procured site-support services (lodging, food, transport, PPE) under fluctuating headcount.

  • You partner across DC Ops, Construction, Recruiting, and Finance, and you've built contractor-to-hire or workforce-development programs.

  • Bonus: Skilled-trades or construction labor sourcing. Liquid cooling / CDU or high-density power trades. Apprenticeship or workforce-grant programs. Multi-site hyperscale buildouts.

     

Salary and Benefits

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

 

Additional benefits include:

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity)

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Data Center Operations Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Operate at the scale of a nation, not a building. Accelerating toward 10s to 100s of GWs by the end of the decade, more than the entire electricity consumption of many countries. You won't just run a data center; you'll run infrastructure the size of a G7.

  • Fly the plane while it's being built. Running flawless operations inside a live construction zone, adapting in real time and turning the pace of build-out into our advantage. You will redefine operational excellence.

  • Write the playbook, don't inherit it. Most operators step into someone else's system. Here you build one, leaving your fingerprints on how the whole company runs. As we scale 100x, you'll set the standards, shape the operating model, and grow the team by the thousands

    .

Role Scope

  • Serve as the on-site SME for data center critical infrastructure, handling escalations across the white space and the supporting facilities.

  • Understand and manage the design limitations and risks of the site, and audit colocation partners and service providers on their maintenance programs and effectiveness.

  • Own the change management process for high-risk maintenance activities in the data center.

  • Act as first responder on-site for incidents, driving resolution with support from engineering and infrastructure SMEs.

  • Partner with colo partners, vendors, and internal teams to keep the site reliable, and feed operational learnings back into design and process.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've operated or led critical-facilities operations in a live data center, owning the physical infrastructure that keeps a site running.

  • You know the critical-infrastructure stack (power and cooling) well enough to be the on-site authority and handle escalations.

  • You run change management for high-risk work and hold partners to a real maintenance standard.

  • You're a calm, capable first responder when something fails at 3am.

  • You audit, document, and improve, leaving the site's operating posture stronger than you found it.

  • Bonus: Hyperscale or colocation operations. Uptime Institute or NFPA familiarity. Critical environment and MOP/EOP experience. Vendor and colo management.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

The Infrastructure Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Turn up gigawatts at the speed of light. First rack to full fabric convergence across tens of thousands of links in weeks, at a new site every few months.

  • Automate yourself out of the cutsheet. ZTP every device, machine-validate every link, and burn down turn-up queues with tooling instead of headcount. Anything done twice by hand becomes software.

  • Make handoff mean flawless. Every optic clean, every link error-tested, every config golden before a training job ever touches the fabric. At this scale, “close enough” is an outage.

     

Role Scope

  • Deploy and validate data center network infrastructure (front-end, back-end, BMS, management): configure switches, install and validate optics, coordinate cabling, and drive deployments to completion.

  • Ensure physical connectivity meets production standards: coordinate fiber remediation, validate insertion loss and OTDR traces, troubleshoot optical-layer issues, and document as-builts.

  • Manage hardware logistics: device staging, rack/stack coordination, RMA, DCIM updates, inventory, and vendor shipments so devices are ready when deployments need them.

  • Partner with DC Operations, ICT, Hardware, and Network Engineering to identify blockers early, escalate decisively, and keep multi-team efforts on track.

  • Maintain cutsheets, as-builts, validation results, and lessons learned, and contribute to the deployment playbook that lets the team scale.

  • Provide operational support during and after deployments: incident response, troubleshooting, and break-fix.

     

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've done hands-on data center network engineering and understand modern fabrics (EVPN/VXLAN, BGP, CLOS), having configured production infrastructure.

  • You thrive in the field, equally comfortable pulling cable, configuring switches, and troubleshooting the optical layer, and you execute with whatever tooling is available.

  • You troubleshoot methodically across physical and logical layers: OTDR traces, insertion loss, BGP sessions, and connectivity through complex topologies.

  • You communicate clearly across technical and non-technical teams, document well, and follow through.

  • You learn fast and take ownership of ramping on new technology, and you'll travel 50 to 60% to onsite deployments.

  • Bonus: AI fabric turn-up experience. Configuration management and automation tooling. Vendor certifications.

 

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Data Center Design Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Lead the design, development, and execution of 10s to 100s of GWs of data centers this decade.

  • Drive the next generation of liquid cooling and electrical distribution systems.

  • Develop and scale first-of-a-kind modular data centers.

  • Influence behind-the-meter designs and planning for multi-GW campuses.

Role Scope

  • Own the civil engineering workstream across a multi-site development portfolio from site screening through permitting and construction completion.

  • Lead civil due diligence for greenfield and conversion sites: topography, drainage, utilities, soils, floodplain, and environmental constraints, flagging fatal flaws and cost risks during site selection.

  • Develop and maintain the civil basis of design, master specs, and standard drawings, and establish grading strategies, earthwork balance, and cut/fill sequences for large campus developments.

  • Structure phased delivery with early work packages (mass grading, site utilities, enablement) to accelerate the critical path.

  • Lead civil permitting strategy across jurisdictions: land disturbance, NPDES/SWPPP, floodplain (CLOMR/LOMR), environmental, and utility permits.

  • Manage external civil consultants from schematic through IFC and coordinate civil scope with structural, MEP, fiber, and architectural teams.

  • You've directed external civil consultants and managed design deliverable quality through IFC.

  • You know grading, earthwork, stormwater, and site utility design cold, plus NPDES and floodplain (FEMA/CLOMR/LOMR) permitting.

  • You've identified civil fatal flaws and quantified cost risk during site selection, not just executed design after the site was chosen.

  • You've coordinated geotechnical investigations and interpreted boring programs into design actions.

  • Bonus: PE license. Hyperscale or energy infrastructure development. Expansive clay, karst, or high water table conditions. MISO/utility interconnection civil coordination. AutoCAD Civil 3D and GIS.

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The People Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Make the office the easiest part of everyone's day. Where people work shapes how they work. You'll own the day-to-day experience of your office so nothing about the space slows anyone down.

  • Replace ad hoc coordination with a consistent bar. As offices grow and multiply, workplace experience can't depend on someone improvising. You'll set the standard that holds across every Fluidstack office.

  • See it, own it, solve it. From a broken monitor to a better lunch option, you handle what comes and fix or escalate it clearly. Hands-on, high ownership, no waiting to be told..

Why This Role Exists

As our offices grow, the day-to-day workplace experience can’t depend on ad hoc coordination. This role exists to ensure each Fluidstack office runs smoothly, consistently, and with a high bar for employee experience.

About the Role

Where people work shapes how people work. You will own the day-to-day experience of your Fluidstack office, everything from how the space looks and functions, to how people feel when they walk in, to the small details that make a workplace feel genuinely cared for.

You’re the person in the building who makes sure things work and when they don’t, you fix them or escalate clearly. People will come to you with everything from a broken monitor to a request for a better lunch option, and you’ll treat both with the same thoughtfulness.

This role is hands-on and high-ownership. You’re not waiting for someone to tell you what needs to happen. You see it, you own it, you solve it.

What You Will Do

First 30 Days

  • Complete onboarding and learn Fluidstack’s workplace standards, vendor landscape, and office-specific context.

  • Shadow the current setup (or audit from scratch if you’re opening a new cadence): space layout, recurring issues, vendor performance, employee sentiment.

  • Build relationships with building management, key vendors, and your local team.

  • Identify 3 quick wins you can deliver in your first month that improve the daily office experience.

By 60 Days

  • Own all vendor relationships for your office: cleaning, catering, maintenance, supplies. Hold them to agreed standards.

  • Implement the shared workplace standards, adapted for your location.

  • Run a lightweight feedback loop with employees in your office. Know what’s working and what isn’t.

  • Manage your office’s operational budget with clear tracking and no surprises.

By 90 Days

  • Your office runs smoothly and consistently. Employees trust that the space will be well-maintained and well-managed.

  • You are the first point of escalation for workplace issues in your office. Problems are resolved quickly and transparently, or escalated with clear context.

  • You have a clear operating rhythm: weekly vendor check-ins, monthly budget reviews, quarterly planning.

  • You proactively surface issues and proposed solutions rather than waiting for direction.

What We Are Looking For

  • A love of details. The things most people don’t notice until they break.

  • Kindness and warmth in how you show up for the people in your building every day.

  • A hospitality mindset. You think about experience, not just maintenance.

  • Clarity, approachability, and precision in communication, especially when things go wrong.

  • You have run an office or workspace before and take pride in making it a place people enjoy being.

  • You manage vendors and service providers with care: expectations are set, performance is tracked, and conversations happen early when standards slip.

  • You’re organized and self-directed. You don’t need a daily task list from a manager to know what needs doing.

  • You welcome non-traditional paths into this work. If you’ve managed spaces, logistics, or operations in any context (hospitality, events, coworking, retail) that counts.

  • You are available to be in-person 5 days per week.

You’ll Thrive Here If You

  • Care about details. The small parts, even the parts no one else sees, matter to you.

  • Care about the human. When you set up a space, you’re thinking about the person who’ll be sitting in it eight hours a day.

  • Enjoy solving problems before anyone notices there was one. You find that satisfying, not thankless.

  • Want to make something really great. A well-run office is a quiet act of care for everyone in it.

What Additive Value Looks Like

  • Experience managing office openings, buildouts, or relocations.

  • Familiarity with workplace technology (access systems, desk booking, AV).

  • A hospitality mindset — you think about experience, not just maintenance.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

The Development Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Find enough land to deploy multiple gigawatts a week. By 2030 we need to bring on multiple gigawatts of new capacity every week, which means securing sites at a pace and scale no one in the industry has operated at. You'll own finding and locking that land ahead of the build.

  • Get power online in months, not years. Most of the clock runs before the lease is ever signed. You'll optimize the pre-signature work, site diligence, permitting, and development, so a site goes from signed lease to live power in under six months.

  • Acquire 10s to 100s of GWs behind the meter. Reaching that scale means generating on-site instead of waiting on grid interconnection. You'll secure the land and behind-the-meter solar generation to get there.

     

Role Scope

  • Lead the site procurement strategy for the US data center portfolio, sourcing and evaluating powered land for large-scale development and negotiating leases with data center operators.

  • Conduct site due diligence: evaluate utility and behind-the-meter power at 200MW+ scale, and assess buildability through title docs, surveys, geotechnical reports, and environmental studies.

  • Understand permitting requirements at each site and their implications for the construction schedule.

  • Maintain relationships with brokers, landowners, and developers so a valid site is never missed, and run vendor due diligence including on-site audits with specialist engineers.

  • Work directly with DC Design to keep sites matched to the latest technical requirements, and own capacity planning and forecasting across clients and regions.

  • Partner with Finance on multi-year infrastructure investment and cost structures, and lead commercial negotiations with landowners and developers.

     

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've worked in real estate with a focus on data centers or other large industrial projects, and you've closed large, complex deals.

  • You assess land viability for data center development fast and rigorously: power, buildability, and permitting.

  • You bring a customer-centric mindset, strong ownership, and proactive problem-solving.

  • You align stakeholders across diverse internal and external teams, and you'll travel 20%+ as projects require.

  • Bonus: Behind-the-meter power evaluation. Hyperscale-scale land deals. Utility interconnection familiarity. Multi-region portfolio planning.

 

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

 

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

About the Role

As a Technical Program Manager for Deployments, you will own the end-to-end program delivery required to bring data center infrastructure and AI clusters online. You will operate in a highly ambiguous environment, coordinating across construction, infrastructure, networking, systems engineering, procurement, and operations teams to ensure deployment readiness and successful go-lives.

This role requires an ownership mindset. You will be expected to move programs forward with sometimes incomplete information, surface and resolve gaps, and ensure progress across teams responsible for construction, networking, hardware, operations, and beyond. While physical installation and construction execution are owned by partner teams, you are accountable for overall delivery outcomes and are expected to fill gaps before they become blockers.

The best candidates for this role bring deep experience in the intersection of data center construction handover and AI/GPU hardware deployment, not just one or the other. You know how construction sequences impact infrastructure readiness, how ICT and CDU work intersect, and how to hold multiple workstreams accountable across time zones and organizational boundaries.

Focus

  • Own program delivery for data hall and AI cluster activation, from planning through operational handoff

  • Coordinate cross-functional teams responsible for construction, infrastructure, network, hardware, ICT, commissioning, and operations execution

  • Translate hyperscale AI/GPU and DLC infrastructure requirements into actionable deployment plans

  • Anticipate downstream impacts of technical sequencing decisions on capacity, schedule, and cluster performance

  • Drive alignment across teams operating at different speeds, scopes, and time zones – including vendor and contractor partners

  • Manage and hold accountable vendors, integration contractors, and third-party service providers across the deployment lifecycle.

  • Operate effectively in ambiguity, making progress with incomplete information and evolving requirements

  • Develop and drive executive-level program status briefings that clearly communicate schedule health, risks, key decisions, and escalations paths

  • Maintain clear, current program artifacts: schedules, RACI matrices, risk registers, decision logs, and deployment runbooks

  • Maintain momentum through changing requirements, tight timelines, and cross-time-zone execution

  • Collaborate closely with SMEs in networking, ICT, commissioning, systems engineerings, product, procurement, operations, and more before execution – not in isolation.

  • Identify and drive process improvements that scale across concurrent builds and future deployments

Must Haves

  • 5+ years experience in delivering complex data center physical infrastructure programs in fast-moving environments

  • Strong understanding of AI/GPU infrastructure, including power density, cooling, networking, and deployment sequencing

  • Demonstrated experience bridging construction handover and cluster deployment: candidates who are network only or construction only will not be a fit

  • Familiarity with how construction, low-voltage, and commissioning activities impact deployment readiness and sequencing

  • Proven ability to lead through influence rather than direct ownership of execution teams

  • Proven ability to manage vendor and contractor relationships, understanding schedule and reputational risks

  • Experience delivering programs across multiple concurrent sites or regions, including planning for staggered milestones

  • Able to develop and present executive-level program status, risk summaries, and key decisions to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders

  • Experience with long-lead procurement processes, and hardware supply chain constraints that affect deployment timelines

  • Actively collaborate with SMEs across multiple domains to validate plans and resolve gaps

  • Comfortable operating with limited process and evolving inputs in a high-growth, intense environment

  • Demonstrated ability to take initiative, fill gaps, and drive execution beyond defined scope, without being directed to do so

  • Able to balance strategic thinking with hands-on program management

  • Comfortable operating outside standard business to meet deployment timelines

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder alignment skills – able to ensure teams at all levels understand priorities and dependencies

  • Strong execution mindset with the ability to balance speed, quality, and risk

  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach to decision making

  • Automation-first mindset with commitment to identifying and implementing process improvements

  • You are willing and able to travel to data center locations, sometimes on short notice; expect to spend up to 60% of your time traveling

Nice To Haves

  • DCD, PMP, CDCPM, CDCMP, CDCP or DCDC Certification(s)

  • ITIL Foundation Certification

  • JIRA, Smartsheet, or similar project tracking and workflow management experience

  • Knowledge of infrastructure automation and deployment tools

  • Experience managing BPO or contract labor pools during large-scale hardware deployment phases

  • Background in material coordination or logistics management at scale during active deployment (receiving, cycle counting, site-to-site transfers)

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity)

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

The IT Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Engineer the systems behind one of the world's largest compute buildouts. Everything runs as code, version-controlled and reproducible, so a new hire, team, or site spins up in minutes instead of days. You'll build internal infrastructure with real engineering rigor and keep it ahead of a company growing 10x.

  • Solve multi-tenancy problems most IT engineers never touch. Fluidstack runs teams, sites, and customers in parallel, and the internal systems have to keep them cleanly separated and secure at speed. You'll own architecture problems usually reserved for product infrastructure, on the inside.

  • Give every employee the speed it takes to reach 10s to 100s of GWs. The faster the company's people move, the faster we get there. You'll own the internal systems and support that keep a 10x workforce unblocked.

Role Scope

  • Provide reliable, hands-on IT support for in-office and remote employees, resolving tickets fast with excellent service.

  • Support the MDM fleet across macOS, iOS, and Windows, and troubleshoot in-office network and A/V systems.

  • Administer and improve Okta and core SaaS tooling: integrations, role-based access controls, and identity hygiene.

  • Run procurement and asset management: coordinate hardware purchasing and track devices across their full lifecycle.

  • Build simple, reliable automations that cut manual work, and write clear documentation for technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Own onboarding and offboarding for employees and contractors, and support access reviews and basic identity security.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've administered Okta (users, groups, app integrations) and managed MDM across macOS and Windows.

  • You know Google Workspace well, with some Office 365 exposure, and you support macOS, iOS, and Windows devices.

  • You build automations to replace manual work, and you reach for code or no-code tools to do it.

  • You write clearly: documentation and knowledge-base content that both technical and non-technical people can use.

  • You bring a security mindset to identity, access, and device management.

  • Bonus: No-code/low-code automation (Okta Workflows, n8n, Zapier, Workato). Scripting (Bash, PowerShell, Python). SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST, or CIS exposure. AI tools, agents, and MCPs (Fluidstack standardizes on Claude). HRIS integrations (Deel, Rippling, Workday). API and webhook fluency.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of stock options.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Stand up a lean finance org for the fastest-growing data center hyperscaler.

  • Own the full stack from vendor invoice to cap table.

  • Own the general ledger function end to end, overseeing journal entries, account reconciliations, and monthly financial statement preparation as the entity structure grows.

  • Lead month-end and year-end close, setting the calendar and holding FP&A, Tax, and Operations to it so the books close on time every cycle.

  • Partner directly with finance leadership and external auditors to keep internal controls tight and the company audit-ready.

  • Build and refine accounting processes and controls as Fluidstack scales, replacing manual workarounds before they become the bottleneck.

     

What We're Looking For

  • You've owned the general ledger function for a company, journal entries, reconciliations, and monthly financials, without a controller reviewing every entry first.

  • You've led month-end or year-end close yourself, holding FP&A, Tax, and cross-functional partners to a calendar instead of chasing them after the fact.

  • You know US GAAP well enough to make the accrual, cutoff, and capitalization calls yourself, and you can explain them clearly to an auditor.

  • You've found a broken accounting process midstream and rebuilt it before it slowed down the close.

  • You work inside NetSuite daily and you're fast and accurate in Excel for anything the system can't handle.

  • You've supported or led an ERP or accounting system implementation, migration, or upgrade, doing hands-on configuration and testing yourself.

  • You run multiple close cycles, audits, and process changes at once without dropping one when another gets hard.

  • You hold a CPA license or an equivalent professional accounting qualification.

  • Bonus: Multi-entity and multi-currency accounting experience. Experience at a high-growth technology or infrastructure company. Direct experience supporting external audits and liaising with auditors. Exposure to intercompany accounting and consolidations.

  • Negotiate pricing, payment terms, lead times, and service levels with vendors, and set a vendor strategy site by site that balances cost, local availability, and continuity of supply.

  • Work with Data Center Operations, inventory control, warehousing, and finance to turn consumption data and build schedules into forecasts and purchase plans.

  • Build the buying playbook for ops spend: standard catalogs, preferred vendors, and ordering thresholds that every new site adopts from day one.

  • You've decided where to consolidate spend with a national supplier and where a local vendor serves a site better, and you managed those vendors to performance.

  • You've bought for a new facility or site launch against a schedule you didn't control, and everything was there on opening day.

  • You work across operations, warehousing, finance, and engineering, and the teams you support call you first when they need something fast.

  • You make purchasing decisions from data: consumption history, lead times, and vendor performance drive your orders, and your records stay clean enough for anyone to audit.

  • Bonus: Data center or critical facilities operations. Auto-replenishment and vendor-managed inventory programs. Procurement and ERP platforms (Zip, NetSuite). Spend analytics and category management.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

    • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

      Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The HSE Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Own safety on gigawatts of high-energy infrastructure, built from zero. Headcount and sites are scaling faster than institutional knowledge can keep up. The gap between a control written on paper and one actually applied in the field is where fatalities happen.

  • Keep a 24/7 workforce running at full intensity, not sidelined by injury. Fatigue, shift work, and high-energy exposure compound on the people running the sites and show up as injuries or claims if no one is tracking them. The work is to catch them first.

  • Keep environmental compliance ahead of the fastest build in the industry. Behind-the-meter generation spans multiple states, each with its own air permit conditions, runtime limits, and reporting deadlines, and the company adds sites faster than any manual compliance model can keep up with.

Role Scope

  • Own HSE across a leased campus another operator controls, where buildings in construction, commissioning, and live operation sit side by side.

  • Review design and commissioning packages for the hazards they build in, and push engineering controls into the drawings before a crew has to work around them.

  • Run hazardous energy control across the site's electrical distribution: switching plans, LOTO, and zero-energy verification as gear lands, tests, and energizes.

  • Own workers compensation and case management at the site, from first report of injury through the carrier and TPA handoff, treatment, and fitness for duty, with transitional duty defined ahead of time so shift-based field crews come back on modified duty in days.

  • Keep injury, illness, and environmental recordkeeping current so the OSHA 300, 300A, and 301 logs, the New York state filings, the stormwater and air permit records, and the claims and near-miss trend view all hold up on inspection and in front of leadership.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've run site safety on a data center or heavy industrial build where construction crews, commissioning, and energized systems shared one campus.

  • You hold OSHA 30 Construction and current First Aid, CPR, and AED certification.

  • You've reviewed design and commissioning packages and gotten an engineering control into the drawings instead of a procedure telling a crew to be careful.

  • You've taken workers compensation claims from first report through closure, and you've worked adjusters, occupational physicians, and clinics hard enough to change how a claim went.

  • You've built or run a return-to-work and transitional duty program that field supervisors actually used, and the return-to-work numbers moved because of it.

  • You've owned OSHA 300, 300A, and 301 recordkeeping through an inspection or an audit where the logs held up.

  • Bonus: Construction safety credentials (CHST, CSP, ASP). Professional engineering licensure (PE). Case and disability management credentials (CCM, CPDM, occupational health RN). New York construction and labor compliance (Industrial Code Rule 23, Labor Law 240 and 241). Claims and injury analytics tooling (Origami, Riskonnect, Intelex).

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Standing up a consistent, compliant process for bringing on and managing contractors across every team and location.

  • Choosing and rolling out the systems that track contractor spend, tenure, and access.

  • Giving hiring managers a clear, fast path to the right workforce solution for their need.

  • Working with Legal and Finance to keep classification and compliance practices current as the program grows.

Role Scope

  • Own day-to-day management of Fluidstack's contractor and extended workforce program, from intake through offboarding.

  • Manage vendor and staffing supplier relationships, holding partners accountable for service quality and responsiveness.

  • Build and maintain compliant processes for worker classification, onboarding, access, and data protection.

  • Advise hiring managers and stakeholders on workforce solutions, weighing cost, speed, compliance, and risk.

  • Improve the systems and workflows behind the program, including vendor management tooling, reporting, and documentation.

  • Partner with Legal, Finance, and IT to resolve escalations and keep the program's controls current as it scales.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 4+ years of experience in contingent workforce, extended workforce, procurement operations, or HR operations.

  • Hands-on experience with a Vendor Management System (VMS) or similar contractor-management tooling.

  • Working knowledge of worker classification, co-employment, and the compliance considerations behind contractor programs.

  • Experience partnering across Legal, Finance, IT, and business stakeholders to resolve workforce issues.

  • A strong operator who solves problems directly and builds solutions rather than waiting on vendors to do it.

  • Comfortable operating with ambiguity and moving with urgency in a fast-changing business.

  • Bonus: Experience scaling a contractor program at a high-growth or infrastructure company. Interest in using automation to reduce manual program work.
