We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Program Controls & PMO Team

The Program Controls & PMO team keeps datacenter design and construction programs running on the current approved baseline, from first drawing to as-built closeout.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Keeping approval workflows moving across design firms, EPCs, vendors, and internal teams without stalling the build.

  • Catching superseded drawings before a site builds off them.

  • Maintaining a revision history and audit trail that commissioning and closeout teams can rely on.

Role Scope

  • Own document control. Own the document control system for datacenter design and construction, covering drawings, specs, submittals, and revisions across many concurrent sites.

  • Run configuration management. Run configuration management so every site is built to the current approved baseline and no team works off a superseded drawing.

  • Set the workflow. Set and enforce the naming, versioning, and approval workflows that keep engineering documents traceable from design through as-built.

  • Manage document flow. Manage the flow of documents between design firms, EPCs, vendors, and internal teams so approvals never stall the build.

  • Maintain the audit trail. Maintain the audit trail and revision history that construction, commissioning, and closeout teams depend on.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've run document control for large engineering or construction programs with many drawings, revisions, and stakeholders in flight at once.

  • You've set up or administered a document control system such as Aconex, Procore, or SharePoint and enforced its workflows.

  • You've managed document flow across external design firms, EPCs, and vendors without letting approvals become the bottleneck.

  • You've owned configuration management and caught the case where a team was about to build off a superseded revision.

  • You keep records so clean that an auditor, a commissioning agent, or a closeout team can trace any document to its current approved version.

  • You catch the missing signature, the wrong revision, or the untracked change before it reaches the field.

  • Bonus: Datacenter, industrial, or mission-critical construction. Aconex, Procore, or Bluebeam. Configuration management on regulated or high-rigor programs. As-built and closeout documentation.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Supply tens of gigawatts of compute, the largest build out of compute in history. Qualify and dual-source across every critical equipment category, with lead-time and capacity thresholds tied directly to the forward build pipeline.

  • Make supply chain the reason we build faster than anyone. Our modular build redefines speed in this industry, and it lives or dies on supply chain. Keep procurement permanently off the critical path so schedule compression stays our advantage, not our constraint.

  • Build the most accurate supply chain prediction modelling that exists. Use the frontier of AI to forecast lead times, demand, and disruption with a precision the industry has never had, and turn that foresight into a structural edge.

Role Scope

  • Own sourcing for mechanical categories feeding manufacturing: steel, fabrications, cooling components, and mechanical assemblies.

  • Lock supply and lead times against the build plan, with capacity commitments that survive demand spikes.

  • Negotiate multi-year agreements that hold price and priority as volumes grow 10x.

What We're Looking For

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've sourced mechanical or fabricated categories for a manufacturer and owned the supplier relationships.

  • You read drawings and specs well enough to challenge a quote line by line.

  • You've qualified new suppliers under time pressure without skipping the steps that matter.

  • You've secured capacity in constrained markets.

  • You manage suppliers on data: on-time delivery, PPM, and lead-time performance.

  • Bonus: Steel and fabrication markets. Cooling and thermal components. Should-cost modeling. Supplier development.

  • You've developed settings for SEL or equivalent platforms hands-on.

  • You've commissioned protection schemes in the field.

  • You've investigated relay operations and found the truth in the event records.

  • Your settings files are managed like the safety-critical code they are.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • You're securing the frontier of AI. The model weights training on our infrastructure are the most valuable and most targeted artifacts in technology, and we're standing up the compute to hold them faster than anyone ever has. A breach isn't a leak, it's the frontier walking out the door.

  • Build the entire security program from scratch. Most leaders inherit someone else's system and spend a career patching it. Here you own it end to end, bare metal to boardroom, as we scale across continents.

  • Your threat surface is measured in gigawatts. The customers running on our infrastructure are building the most consequential technology in human history, and being responsible for the physical and logical security of that work makes everything else feel small.

Role Scope

  • Design and defend the network security architecture across data centers, corp, and cloud: segmentation, firewalls, and east-west controls at gigawatt scale.

  • Build network detection: telemetry, flow analysis, and alerting across training fabrics, OT networks, and the WAN.

  • Harden the OT and BMS side, where the network touches physical plant, against threats most security teams never see.

  • Automate network security controls so new sites inherit the architecture on day one.

What We're Looking For

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've secured production networks at scale, and you read a packet capture as comfortably as a dashboard.

  • You've designed segmentation for environments that mix IT, OT, and high-value compute.

  • You've deployed and tuned NDR or flow-based detection that found real intrusions.

  • You work infrastructure-as-code: your firewall rules live in a repo, not a GUI.

  • You've partnered with network engineering without becoming the department of no.

  • Bonus: OT and ICS security. Data center or cloud provider environments. BGP and routing security. Zeek or Suricata.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Partner with strategic finance, legal, and commercial teams to structure and account for complex, high-value transactions correctly the first time.

What We're Looking For

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've written technical accounting memos on complex areas such as revenue recognition, leases, business combinations, or equity, and they held up under audit scrutiny.

  • You've built accounting policies, processes, or controls from scratch rather than maintaining a mature function.

  • You've worked through the accounting for genuinely novel or complex transactions where the precedent was thin.

  • You explain technical accounting conclusions clearly enough that non-accountants can act on them.

About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Security Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • You're securing the frontier of AI. The model weights training on our infrastructure are the most valuable and most targeted artifacts in technology, and we're standing up the compute to hold them faster than anyone ever has. A breach isn't a leak, it's the frontier walking out the door.

  • Build the entire security program from scratch. Most leaders inherit someone else's system and spend a career patching it. Here you own it end to end, bare metal to boardroom, as we scale across continents.

  • Your threat surface is measured in gigawatts. The customers running on our infrastructure are building the most consequential technology in human history, and being responsible for the physical and logical security of that work makes everything else feel small.

Role Scope

  • Own end-to-end security for every server in the bare metal fleet, from supply chain and provisioning through hardening, operation, and secure decommissioning.

  • Design and maintain hardened golden OS images with automated vulnerability scanning, patch pipelines, and configuration-drift detection.

  • Define and enforce the BMC security model (access control, credential rotation, audit logging, firmware integrity) for one of the most under-defended surfaces in the industry.

  • Partner with network engineering on micro-segmentation, IDS/IPS, and firewall architecture, applying zero-trust from the top-of-rack up.

  • Implement data-at-rest encryption, key management, and secure storage access at fleet scale, and build the automation that makes secure-by-default the path of least resistance.

  • Lead threat modeling and security reviews for new hardware platforms and network designs, and respond to incidents touching the physical fleet.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've worked in information security or infrastructure engineering with a strong focus on bare metal, IaaS, or high-scale cloud infrastructure.

  • You harden Linux deeply (SELinux, AppArmor, kernel-level security) and command network security (TCP/IP, VPNs, firewall rulesets, zero-trust).

  • You implement encryption in practice, including disk-level (LUKS) and hardware-level, and you understand HSMs and trusted computing (TPM/TXT).

  • You automate fluently in Python, Go, or Rust, with configuration management (Ansible, Puppet, Chef).

  • You work well across engineering teams and communicate security decisions clearly.

  • Bonus: BMC platforms (OpenBMC, iDRAC, iLO). Hardware root of trust and secure boot. Compliance standards (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP). CISSP, OSCP, or CEH.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.


Applicant Privacy Notice
AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Data Center Operations Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Operate at the scale of a nation, not a building. The fleet you run will draw more power than some countries, on the way to tens of gigawatts.

  • Fly the plane while it's being built. Sites come online in pieces, and you keep the live ones running flawlessly while construction continues around them.

  • Write the playbook, don't inherit it. No prior operations org has run at this speed and scale, so the standards you set become the standard.

Role Scope

  • Run the building management and controls systems (BMS, SCADA, EPMS) that keep live gigawatt-scale data centers cooling and powered in real time.

  • Own real-time load and thermal control across sites coming online in pieces, keeping the live halls running flawlessly while construction continues around them.

  • Write the operating procedures, alarm response runbooks, and control sequences that become the standard for every site that follows.

  • Diagnose and resolve controls faults on the floor, from a misbehaving chiller sequence to a breaker mis-operation, before they touch a training run.

  • Tune control sequences and setpoints to hold PUE and reliability targets as load ramps and hardware generations change.

What We're Looking For

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've operated the controls for live mission-critical facilities, data center, industrial, or power, and kept them running through faults, ramps, and construction next door.

  • You know BMS, SCADA, and EPMS platforms deep enough to diagnose a bad sequence or a misconfigured point, not just read the alarm.

  • You've written operating procedures and alarm response runbooks that other operators actually run.

  • You've resolved a real controls fault under pressure, on a live floor, with load on the line.

  • You tune control sequences and setpoints and can explain the tradeoff between reliability, efficiency, and cost.

  • You catch the drifting sensor or the wrong setpoint before it becomes an outage.

  • Bonus: Hyperscale or colocation data center operations. Liquid cooling controls. Electrical power monitoring systems. Behind-the-meter generation. Building the controls standards for a new fleet.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The It Team

  • Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Engineer the systems behind one of the world's largest compute buildouts. Everything runs as code, version-controlled and reproducible, so a new hire, team, or site spins up in minutes instead of days. You'll build internal infrastructure with real engineering rigor and keep it ahead of a company growing 10x.

  • Solve multi-tenancy problems most IT engineers never touch. Fluidstack runs teams, sites, and customers in parallel, and the internal systems have to keep them cleanly separated and secure at speed. You'll own architecture problems usually reserved for product infrastructure, on the inside.

  • Give every employee the speed it takes to reach tens of gigawatts. The faster the company's people move, the faster we get to tens of gigawatts. You'll own the internal systems and support that keep a 10x workforce unblocked.

Role Scope

  • Build and run the on-site IT infrastructure at gigawatt-scale data center campuses, from corporate network and Wi-Fi to badge systems, conference rooms, and edge compute, so a new site is operational the day the first team arrives.

  • Automate provisioning of endpoints, identity, and access across a workforce growing 10x, so device setup and offboarding run as version-controlled code rather than manual tickets.

  • Own the multi-site IT stack that keeps teams, contractors, and customers cleanly separated and secure, coordinating with the security team on access controls and network segmentation.

  • Stand up repeatable IT deployment runbooks for each new campus so the tenth site comes online faster and cleaner than the first.

  • Resolve on-site incidents and unblock field and construction teams directly, closing the gap between a reported issue and a working system in hours, not days.

What We're Looking For

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've built and run IT infrastructure across multiple physical sites, standing up networks, identity, and endpoint management from nothing rather than inheriting a mature environment.

  • You've automated IT operations with code (scripting, infrastructure-as-code, MDM policy as code) so that a task done twice by hand became software.

  • You've owned identity and access management (SSO, SCIM, directory services) for a fast-growing organization without letting access sprawl or offboarding gaps accumulate.

  • You've been the person field, construction, or operations teams call when systems are down on site, and you've resolved incidents under time pressure with people waiting on you.

  • You've designed multi-tenant or segmented network environments that kept separate teams, sites, or customers secure without slowing anyone down.

  • You write documentation and runbooks clear enough that the next engineer can stand up a site without asking you how.

  • Bonus: Data center or industrial site IT experience. Hands-on networking (BGP, VLANs, firewalls) at scale. Okta, Jamf, or Intune administration. Security or compliance framework exposure (SOC 2, ISO 27001).

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • You catch a lead-time or capacity problem in the data weeks before it becomes a schedule problem.

  • You write analysis clearly enough that a buyer or an executive can act on it without a follow-up meeting.

  • You've partnered with procurement, operations, or finance and shipped analysis that changed what they bought or when.

  • You check your own numbers and you know when a forecast is guessing rather than telling you something.

  • Bonus: Supply chain, procurement, or logistics analytics. Data center or hardware equipment categories. SQL and Python for data work. Statistical or machine-learning forecasting methods. Scaling analysis inside a high-growth operation.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

Role Scope

  • Source and lock powered land and brownfield sites that can deliver hundreds of megawatts to gigawatts of capacity, ahead of the build pipeline.

  • Negotiate land purchase, lease, and option agreements with landowners, developers, and utilities who don't share our timeline.

  • Diligence power availability, interconnection queue position, substation proximity, and deliverability before a site advances past LOI.

  • Build and manage a pipeline of powered-land opportunities across multiple regions, and kill weak sites fast so capital and attention go to the ones that pencil.

  • Hand off secured sites to development and construction with clean title, a proven power path, and complete diligence so no surprise stalls mobilization.

What We're Looking For

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've personally sourced and closed land or site acquisitions where getting power to the site was the constraint that made or broke the deal.

  • You've negotiated purchase, lease, and option agreements directly with landowners, developers, and utilities.

  • You've read an interconnection queue, a utility capacity map, or a substation study and known whether a site could actually get power and when.

  • You've run land diligence end to end across title, zoning, environmental, and power path, and caught the problem that would have killed the deal after signing.

  • You've managed a multi-site pipeline and walked away from sites that didn't pencil without sinking months into them first.

  • You move fast against counterparties who don't, and you've closed a site while a competitor was still scheduling the first call.

  • Bonus: Datacenter, industrial, or large-scale energy site acquisition. Utility interconnection and power markets. Brownfield or greenfield development. Title, entitlement, and land-use diligence.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law.   • Build the reporting rhythm that gives delivery leads and executives a single source of truth on schedule, budget, and risk across all active programs.

  • Drive the integrated risk register from identification to mitigation, surfacing schedule and cost exposure weeks before it lands on the critical path.

  • Stand up the program controls tooling and standards that let a new site plug into the same schedule, cost, and reporting model on day one.

  • Coordinate across construction, procurement, design, and commissioning to keep interdependencies visible and handoffs clean.

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've owned program controls, schedule, cost, and risk, across a portfolio of large capital projects running at the same time.

  • You've built a reporting cadence that executives actually trust to make decisions, not a deck no one reads.

  • You catch schedule slips and cost overruns weeks before they surface, because your integrated schedule and risk register are live, not stale.

  • You've stood up program controls standards or tooling from scratch and gotten multiple teams to actually use them.

  • You coordinate across construction, procurement, and design without losing track of the interdependencies that break schedules.

  • You write clearly enough to turn a tangled program status into a decision and a next step for a delivery lead or a CEO.

  • Bonus: Data center, mission-critical, or large industrial construction. Primavera P6 or equivalent scheduling at portfolio scale. Earned value management. Modular or repeatable build programs.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

  • Lead the design, development, and execution of 10s to 100s of GWs of data centers this decade.

  • Drive the next generation of liquid cooling and electrical distribution systems.

  • Develop and scale first-of-a-kind modular data centers.

  • Influence behind-the-meter designs and planning for multi-GW campuses.

Role Scope

  • Own environmental and civil engineering for data center site development: stormwater, grading and drainage, erosion control, and environmental constraints, from first site walk through permits in hand.

  • Drive environmental permitting (SWPPP and construction stormwater, wetlands and waters permits, land disturbance approvals) through agencies and consultants on schedules measured in weeks.

  • Screen prospective sites for fatal flaws (wetlands, floodplains, protected species habitat, contamination findings) before the company commits capital, and kill bad sites early.

  • Manage third-party civil and environmental consultants, holding deliverables to schedule and rejecting work that isn't permit-ready.

  • Coordinate civil design (grading, site utilities, roads, drainage) with structural and architectural scopes so site packages issue complete and build without rework.

What We're Looking For

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've taken industrial or large commercial sites through environmental permitting yourself: you wrote or directed the SWPPP, the delineations, and the applications, and agencies approved them.

  • You've screened raw land for development risk and made the call that saved a project from a fatal flaw.

  • You've worked directly with regulators (the Corps, state environmental agencies, county authorities) and secured approvals without slipping the schedule.

  • You've managed AE and environmental consultants and sent work back when it wasn't ready.

  • You read grading and drainage plans fluently and redline them with specifics, elevations and pipe sizes rather than general comments.

  • You've sequenced environmental compliance against construction speed, satisfying the permit while keeping the site moving.

  • Bonus: PE license (civil or environmental). Data center, solar, or heavy industrial site development. Multi-state permitting. Civil 3D or hydrology modeling tools. Karst, floodplain, or brownfield site experience.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Role Scope

  • Produce civil drawing sets for data center site development: grading, drainage, erosion control, utilities, and site plans, from engineer redlines to issued-for-construction.

  • Turn drawing revisions around inside a day during permitting and construction, when a submittal date or an open RFI is waiting on the sheet.

  • Build and maintain the civil CAD standards (templates, layers, detail library) so every site's drawing set is consistent and the next project starts ahead.

  • Coordinate civil sheets against structural and architectural models to catch clashes on paper before they cost time in the field.

  • Prepare permit exhibits, plats, and agency-requested revisions that keep submittals moving without pulling engineers off design work.

What We're Looking For

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've drafted civil construction documents in Civil 3D or AutoCAD that were issued for construction and built from.

  • You've built surfaces, grading, corridors, and pipe networks in Civil 3D yourself, from survey data to finished sheets.

  • You've turned engineer redlines into finished sheets on same-day deadlines and kept the set consistent while doing it.

  • You keep drawing sets internally airtight: callouts resolve, matchlines align, and every referenced detail exists.

  • You've worked deadlines where a missed submittal slips a permit, and the sheet was ready.

  • You've set up or maintained CAD standards that other drafters followed.

  • Bonus: Data center, industrial, or utility-scale solar site work. Revit or Navisworks coordination. Survey data processing. Permit exhibit and plat preparation. Erosion control and SWPPP drawing experience.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Data Center Operations Team

The Data Center Operations team keeps live, mission-critical facilities running while the buildings around them are still being built.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Operate 480V to 15kV+ electrical distribution, generators, switchgear, and UPS systems in facilities running live AI training workloads where downtime is not an option.

  • Run safe switching, lockout/tagout, and energization procedures in buildings where construction, commissioning, and production operations overlap on the same electrical systems.

  • Build the operating procedures, emergency response playbooks, and operator training programs for facilities that are scaling faster than any standard runbook covers.

  • Drive incident response and root-cause analysis on electrical events so the same failure never takes capacity offline twice.

Role Scope

  • Own day-to-day operation and troubleshooting of medium and high-voltage electrical distribution, including switchgear, generators, UPS systems, and associated protection and controls, in live data center environments.

  • Run switching operations, lockout/tagout, and energization work to NFPA 70E and arc flash standards, with documentation rigorous enough to stand up to a safety audit.

  • Lead electrical incident response on shift and on call, isolating faults, restoring power, and producing root-cause reports that change how the facility is operated.

  • Build and maintain SOPs, MOPs, and EOPs for electrical systems, and keep them accurate as new capacity comes online.

  • Drive alarm monitoring and response through BMS and EPMS platforms, tuning thresholds and escalation paths so real problems surface before they become outages.

  • Train and mentor junior operators to the point where they can run switching and response procedures without you in the room.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've spent years operating and troubleshooting 480V to 15kV+ electrical distribution equipment hands-on in live hyperscale or large colocation data centers.

  • You have deep working experience with generators, medium-voltage switchgear, UPS systems, and the BMS/EPMS platforms that monitor them.

  • You know NFPA 70E, arc flash boundaries, and lockout/tagout procedures well enough to write them, enforce them, and catch a shortcut before it becomes an incident.

  • You have a track record of shift-based or on-call critical facility operations, and you've been the person who restores power at 3am.

  • You operate independently. Given a new facility with incomplete documentation, you build the procedures rather than wait for them.

  • You've trained junior operators and can raise a team's standard, not just your own output.

  • You're comfortable running live operations inside an active build environment where construction and commissioning share the floor with production load.

  • Bonus: NETA certification, journeyman or master electrician license, or commissioning experience on greenfield data center electrical systems.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Decision Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Automate the delivery of gigawatts. Every process that takes AI infrastructure from land to live compute becomes software: schedules, decisions, and todos generated from a live knowledge graph instead of chased by hand.

  • Forward-deploy beside the experts. Product teams sit with quality managers, sourcing leads, and deployment engineers on factory floors and sites, and turn their judgment into systems that reach every unit.

  • Deliver every supercomputer faster than the last. Dozens of concurrent projects feed one graph, so every lesson learned at one site becomes a preventive check at all of them.

Role Scope

  • Build the schedule that runs the portfolio: one template schedule per building type, instantiated per project, with every activity tied to the materials it consumes, so need-by dates for switchgear, transformers, and cooling fall out of the critical path instead of a spreadsheet, and a slip in permitting reprices the procurement calendar the same hour.

  • Turn the site into structured data: work packages, contractor field entries, rack placements, cable runs, and QA inspections land as records tied to the design revision they were built against, percent complete is computed from evidence rather than reported on a call, and the customer sees delivered against committed without anyone assembling a deck.

  • Ship change orders as a workflow, not an email chain: scope, cost, and schedule impact drafted from the design delta, routed through legal, finance, and the general contractor with the approval trail attached, and the bill of materials and schedule updated the moment the order is signed.

  • Make the design the source of truth: ingest building information models straight into the bill of materials with a reviewable diff on every revision, generate submittal requirements per spec section, and keep sites, buildings, and data halls as one canonical record that every downstream system reads instead of copies.

  • Ship commissioning as software: test procedures generated per asset from the design revision across all five levels, results landing as evidence against the asset they tested, energization gates that check themselves, and handover that opens on proof instead of a signature.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've shipped production code in Go, Python, or TypeScript, and you pick up whatever language the problem demands.

  • You identify problems, design the solution, and ship it without waiting for direction or approval.

  • You've moved fast under deadline while leaving foundations that other engineers extended after you moved on.

  • You've earned credibility with people who build physical things: construction leads, field engineers, schedulers, or commissioning agents, and driven adoption of your software inside their real deadlines.

  • Your product taste shows in what you've shipped: interfaces field crews call obvious, and workflows that match how the work actually happens.

  • Bonus: Construction tech or project controls (P6, schedule engines, critical path). BIM, IFC, or Revit data models. Commissioning, BMS/EPMS, or controls protocols. Document control and submittal workflows. Graph data models. Computer vision on site imagery.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive total compensation package (cash + equity)

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Retirement plan

  • Generous PTO policy

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

The Decision Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Automate the delivery of gigawatts. Every process that takes AI infrastructure from land to live compute becomes software: schedules, decisions, and todos generated from a live knowledge graph instead of chased by hand.

  • Forward-deploy beside the experts. Product teams sit with quality managers, sourcing leads, and deployment engineers on factory floors and sites, and turn their judgment into systems that reach every unit.

  • Deliver every supercomputer faster than the last. Dozens of concurrent projects feed one graph, so every lesson learned at one site becomes a preventive check at all of them.

Role Scope

  • Turn the bill of materials into the order book: every template bill carries the price and lead time of each line, every project bill locks against a building, and every purchase order derives from it, so tens of billions of dollars of GPUs, optics, switchgear, and cooling are ordered from one source of truth instead of a spreadsheet.

  • Close the loop from receiving to payment: every delivery matches a purchase order line, every warehouse bin knows its serial numbers, cycle counts are scored against an accuracy gate, and finance three-way matches from the same record, so the question "did we get what we paid for" has one answer instead of three.

  • Ship manufacturing as software before the factory opens: manufacturing bills of materials, engineering change notices, and the drawing tree live in one model, inspection and test plans and first article procedures generate per asset from the design revision, and a failed check opens a nonconformance with the evidence attached and rescores the vendor.

  • Embed with sourcing leads, quality managers, factory operators, and warehouse teams, on their floors and in their vendor calls, and turn their judgment into the systems that decide the order schedule, the cash demand by month, and the payment schedule the company plans against.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've shipped production code in Go, Python, or TypeScript, and you pick up whatever language the problem demands.

  • You identify problems, design the solution, and ship it without waiting for direction or approval.

  • You've moved fast under deadline while leaving data models and foundations that other engineers extended after you moved on.

  • You've earned credibility with operators in factories, warehouses, or procurement, and driven adoption of your software inside their real deadlines, like a live production run or a quarter-end close.

  • Your product taste shows in what you've shipped: interfaces the floor calls obvious, and workflows that match how the work actually happens.

  • Bonus: MES, ERP, WMS, or TMS systems. BOM lineage, engineering change control, and serialized component traceability. Supplier quality (NCRs, CAPA, FAI). Three-way match and receiving reconciliation. LLM extraction over vendor documents. High-volume hardware supply chains.

Benefits:

  • Competitive total compensation package (cash + equity)

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Retirement plan

  • Generous PTO policy

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

The Capacity Delivery Program Team

The Capacity Delivery Program team turns signed capacity commitments into energized, GPU-ready data centers on dates our customers have already bet their roadmaps on.

Examples of key problems the team is working on:

  • Build and maintain integrated CPM schedules across greenfield data center builds where design, procurement, construction, and commissioning all run in parallel.

  • Find and close schedule compression opportunities on critical paths measured in days, not months, from long-lead equipment delivery to Day 1 energization.

  • Track cost and field productivity against baselines rigorous enough to catch overruns while they are still recoverable.

  • Give delivery leads and executives a single, defensible source of truth on where every project stands and what threatens the date.

Role Scope

  • Own the P6 CPM schedule for one or more greenfield data center builds, from baseline through closeout, with logic tight enough to survive scrutiny from GCs, owners, and executives.

  • Run cost and productivity tracking against budget and baseline, surfacing variances with the data to back them before they become claims or slips.

  • Drive schedule compression on the critical path, quantifying every recovery option in days and dollars rather than padding buffers.

  • Lead schedule reviews with GC and trade partner schedulers, challenging float sequestration, bad logic, and optimistic durations before they get baselined.

  • Build the reporting cadence (look-aheads, earned value, milestone dashboards) that lets delivery leadership make Day-1-versus-Day-2 tradeoffs with real numbers.

  • Close out projects with as-built schedules and cost records complete enough to hold up under an owner audit and feed the next build's baseline.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 4+ years of hands-on P6 CPM scheduling and cost controls as the person building and owning the schedule, not managing a vendor who does.

  • Greenfield hyperscale or data center build experience, or comparably complex construction programs of $500M or more.

  • Expert in Primavera P6, Bluebeam, and the MS Suite; you can rebuild a broken schedule logic network yourself, not just review one.

  • A track record you can quantify: dollars saved, days compressed, milestones pulled in, with the numbers to prove it.

  • You communicate concisely and defend schedule decisions under scrutiny, in writing and in the room with GCs and executives.

  • You compress schedules instead of padding them; you can articulate what has to be true for Day 1 versus what can wait for Day 2.

  • Based in Austin or willing to relocate, and authorized to work in the US without sponsorship or visa transfer.

  • Bonus: direct experience on hyperscaler data center programs or with a tier-one GC delivering them.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Modular Team

The Modular team designs and builds factory-produced, serialized data center modules that ship as manufactured products, not construction projects.

Examples of key problems the team is working on:

  • Turn first-of-a-kind modular data center designs into repeatable, serialized production builds without losing engineering intent between revisions.

  • Keep design iteration fast while units at different build states move through the fab floor, in inventory, and at site simultaneously.

  • Integrate power, cooling, and structural subsystems into a single releasable product definition that manufacturing, supply chain, and quality can all build against.

  • Close the loop between as-designed, as-built, and as-maintained configurations so field units can be serviced and upgraded against accurate records.

Role Scope

  • Own the release process from engineering to production: drawings, BOMs, and specs complete, approved, and released to manufacturing at the right revision, every time.

  • Run configuration and change management: administer ECOs and ECNs, control revision history, and disposition changes across in-flight units, inventory, and supplier orders with serialized modules at different build states.

  • Keep BOM integrity across systems: engineering and manufacturing BOMs accurate, the PLM system of record syncing cleanly to ERP and MES, and discrepancies between as-designed, as-built, and as-maintained resolved rather than logged.

  • Gate release readiness: drawing checks, tolerance and spec completeness, long-lead procurement flags, and DFM feedback from the fab floor confirmed incorporated before anything releases.

  • Drive release communication across design, supply chain, quality, and production: publish release schedules and change impacts so procurement and the shop floor never build to stale revisions.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 8+ years of experience in release and configuration management for manufactured hardware, including ECO administration, BOM integrity, and PLM, ERP, and MES systems.

  • You've owned release or configuration management for manufactured hardware: modules, vehicles, machinery, or similar serialized products.

  • You've administered ECOs across live production and know how to disposition a change across units already in build, sitting in inventory, and already shipped, including deciding effectivity and living with the consequences.

  • Your BOMs reconcile: as-designed, as-built, and as-maintained stay in sync because you keep them that way, not because nobody has checked.

  • You catch immature releases before the floor does: incomplete drawings, missing tolerances, and unspecified requirements don't get past you.

  • You've untangled an as-designed vs. as-built mess at a company scaling faster than its release discipline, and you know exactly what breaks when that discipline is missing.

  • You work across disciplines instead of throwing problems over walls: design, supply chain, quality, and production all trust your revision state because you keep them informed before it matters.

  • Bonus: hands-on with PLM platforms (Arena, Teamcenter, Windchill), ERP and MES integration (NetSuite, SAP, or similar), drawing standards (ASME Y14.5), or a manufacturing or quality engineering background.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

The Modular Team

The Modular team designs and industrializes factory-built data center units, turning first-of-a-kind designs into repeatable products the factory can build again and again.

Examples of key problems the team is working on:

  • Take modular data center designs from engineering concept to fabrication-ready packages that a shop can build without a phone call.

  • Detail the structures, skids, and piping systems inside each unit down to the weld and bolt level.

  • Absorb rapid engineering changes across in-flight units without losing revision control or slowing the factory.

  • Build the modeling standards, part libraries, and templates that make every next unit faster to detail than the last.

Role Scope

  • Produce the detailed mechanical and structural models and drawings the factory builds from: structures, skids, piping, and assemblies, fully detailed with nothing left to interpretation.

  • Detail steel and mechanical systems to fabrication level: connections, penetrations, pipe spools, and BOM-linked parts, complete enough that a fitter never has to guess.

  • Turn engineering changes into updated, released drawing packages in days, not weeks, with clean revision tracking throughout.

  • Own model hygiene: build and enforce the standards, libraries, and templates that make each subsequent unit faster to detail and harder to get wrong.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 8+ years of experience detailing structural steel, skids, piping, or modular assemblies for fabrication, including weld symbols, connections, and BOM-linked drawing packages.

  • You've detailed for fabrication: structural steel, skids, piping, or modular assemblies, in a fab shop, skid builder, or modular manufacturing environment.

  • Shops build from your drawings without calling. Your packages carry the weld symbols, bolt callouts, and dimensions a fitter actually needs.

  • You model to standards and keep library discipline: parts, templates, and naming conventions stay clean under pressure.

  • You handle revision storms without version chaos. When engineering changes land, the released package is always the right one.

  • You know how things get made: welds, bends, tolerances, and the clearances real fabricators need to fit up, weld out, and inspect.

  • You know what gets red-lined when it's missing, and your detailing has changed because of it.

  • Bonus: Tekla or Advance Steel, plant and BIM modeling (Revit, Plant 3D), AWS weld symbols and AISC detailing standards, or BIM coordination experience.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Produce installation-level electrical and controls packages that fabricators and electricians build from without engineering support on the floor.

  • Standardize the design system, libraries, templates, and BOM structures, so every unit is faster to detail and build than the last.

  • Absorb rapid engineering changes across in-flight units without breaking configuration control.

Role Scope

  • Produce the detailed electrical and controls models and drawings the factory builds from: panels, raceway, cable schedules, and terminations fully detailed, no gaps left to field interpretation.

  • Detail to installation level: conduit and cable tray runs, panel layouts, wiring diagrams, and BOM-linked parts accurate enough that the shop orders and builds straight from the package.

  • Turn engineering changes into updated, released packages in days, with revisions tracked cleanly so no one builds from a stale sheet.

  • Own the model's cleanliness: build and maintain the standards, symbol libraries, and templates that make the next unit faster to detail than the last.

  • Close out drawing issues at the source, fixing the template or standard that caused the question, not just the sheet.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 8+ years of experience detailing electrical and controls packages for fabrication or modular assemblies, including wiring diagrams, cable schedules, and installation-level drawings.

  • You've detailed electrical or controls packages for fabrication or modular assemblies, in a panel shop, UL 508A builder, or industrial automation integrator.

  • You live in an electrical CAD platform; wiring diagrams and cable schedules are your daily output, not an occasional task.

  • Shops and electricians build from your drawings without calling. When they do call, you change the template or standard so that category of call never happens again.

  • You model to standards and maintain library discipline: you build and curate symbol libraries and templates instead of just consuming them.

  • You handle revision storms without version chaos; the released package is always the one being built.

  • You know how things get installed: bend radii, terminations, and the clearances real electricians need, and your drawings reflect it.

  • Bonus: AutoCAD Electrical or EPLAN, plant and BIM modeling (Revit, Plant 3D), panel and wiring diagram standards, and BIM coordination experience.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Modular Team

The Modular team is designing a factory-built data center product for the largest AI compute buildout in history: engineered once, built repeatedly, and deployed faster than site-built construction allows.

Examples of key problems the team is working on:

  • Move data center construction from the field to the factory: designs that ship as pre-terminated assemblies and harnesses instead of site-pulled wire.

  • Resolve the collisions between electrical, mechanical, and structural systems inside a module envelope where every routing path, penetration, and tolerance is contested.

  • Turn first-article builds and factory feedback into design revisions fast enough that each unit builds cleaner than the last.

  • Keep a repeatable product under configuration control while the design iterates between prototypes, factory runs, and field deployments.

Role Scope

  • Engineer the electrical systems of the modular product, power distribution, grounding, and controls integration, from concept through released drawings.

  • Own the one-lines, panel schedules, and cable and raceway design, drawn to a standard the factory installs from and the field connects to without hand-holding.

  • Solve the integration problems where electrical meets structure and mechanical: routing, penetrations, and tolerances where the disciplines collide.

  • Run electrical support for the factory and the field: RFIs answered same-day, and every fix engineered into the next revision instead of living as a redline.

  • Drive prototyping and validation through mockups, fit checks, and first-article reviews you attend in person.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 8+ years of experience in electrical engineering for modular construction, prefab power systems, or critical facilities, including power distribution, grounding, and controls integration.

  • You've engineered electrical systems hands-on for complex physical products, modular construction, or critical facilities: prefab power skids, switchgear OEM products, modular data centers, or repeatable critical-facility work at an EPC.

  • You've supported production launches of your own designs, from first article through repeat builds.

  • You design for factory install, not field construction: you think in harnesses and pre-terminated assemblies rather than site-pulled wire.

  • Your drawings build clean. Fabricators and electricians rarely call, and when they do, you fix the drawing rather than explain it.

  • You work across disciplines instead of throwing problems over walls: when your raceway hits a structural member, you're in the room resolving it.

  • You iterate fast without losing configuration control, so every unit on the floor is built from a known revision.

  • Bonus: PE license, fluency in electrical codes and panel standards (NEC, UL 508A), data center power distribution experience, electrical CAD mastery (AutoCAD Electrical, Revit), and strong DFM instincts.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

  • Engineer a modular data center product that survives fabrication, trucking, craning, and stacking without field rework.

  • Resolve the collisions between structure and MEP: penetrations, attachment points, and tolerances where disciplines meet in a tight envelope.

  • Compress the loop from factory and field issues to engineered fixes in the next design revision.

  • Prove designs with physical mockups, fit checks, and first-article reviews before they scale to production.

Role Scope

  • Engineer the structural systems of the modular product, frames, enclosures, and lifting and transport structures, from concept through released fabrication drawings.

  • Own the structural calcs and load paths so modules survive fabrication, shipping, rigging, and stacking without redesign.

  • Solve the integration problems where structure meets MEP: penetrations, attachment points, and tolerances where the disciplines collide.

  • Run structural support for the factory and field, answering RFIs same-day and engineering fixes into the next revision.

  • Drive prototyping and validation through mockups, fit checks, and first-article reviews you attend in person.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 8+ years of experience in structural engineering for modular construction or heavy fabrication, including frames and enclosures, load paths, and lifting and transport structures.

  • You've engineered structures hands-on for complex physical products, modular construction, or heavy fabrication (modules, trailers, skids, container conversions).

  • You've taken a steel or sheet metal product from concept through fabrication, not just analyzed someone else's design.

  • You've supported production launches of your own designs and stayed accountable through first articles.

  • You treat transport loads, lifting points, and stacking as first-class design constraints, not afterthoughts checked at the end.

  • Your drawings build clean: fabricators rarely call, and when they do, you fix the drawing.

  • You work across disciplines instead of throwing problems over walls, and you iterate fast without losing configuration control.

  • Bonus: PE license, steel and sheet metal design depth, structural detailing standards (AISC, AWS), 3D CAD mastery (SolidWorks, Inventor, Revit), and strong DFM instincts.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Own the global monthly and quarterly close for payroll and benefits, accounts payable, and all operating expenses here at Fluidstack; partnering daily with FP&A, Revenue Ops, Financial Reporting, Tax, Treasury, IT, Sales Ops, and Global Workplace Services to close accurately and on time under US GAAP.

  • Run the accounting stack in NetSuite, VisualLease, Zip, Navan, and Brex, keeping payroll, and expense data clean and audit-ready as transaction volume scales.

  • Lead and mentor the corporate accounting team and the offshore shared services team, building the processes that let a lean team keep pace with headcount and transaction growth.

  • You've worked across Big 4 public accounting and in-house corporate accounting, and you've operated within a broader CAO organization beyond just the accounting function.

  • You've written accounting memos that resolve ambiguous, judgment-heavy transactions and stood behind those conclusions with external auditors.

  • You've run a close that holds up under SOX and Big 4 external audit requirements, with the documentation and controls to prove it.

  • You've used AI or automation to cut manual work out of an accounting process, and you can point to what changed as a result.

  • You manage up and down at once: aligning executives on accounting positions while mentoring a team, including an offshore shared services team.

  • Hands-on experience with NetSuite, VisualLease, Zip, Navan, or Brex specifically. SEC reporting exposure at a public company.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Product Engineering, Photovoltaics (PV) Team

The PV Product Engineering team is building a captive photovoltaic supply chain to power gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure, starting at the cell.

Examples of key problems the team is working on:

  • Select and commit to a silicon cell architecture (TOPCon, HJT, or back-contact) and the efficiency and cost trajectory that decision locks in for years.

  • Build the loss-analysis and efficiency entitlement framework that tells every process and device engineer where the next basis point of efficiency comes from.

  • Stand up pilot line partnerships and a technology transfer path from pilot to production that survives contact with a real fab.

  • Set cell procurement specs and co-engineer with suppliers so the buildout keeps moving while our own line comes up.

Role Scope

  • Own the selection of Fluidstack's cell architecture (TOPCon, HJT, or back-contact) and the technology roadmap behind it, with an efficiency and cost trajectory you can defend to a CEO and a fab partner alike.

  • Build the loss-analysis framework and efficiency entitlement model, decomposed across recombination, optical, and resistive losses, rigorous enough that every process and device engineer knows exactly where their next basis point comes from.

  • Direct the technical agenda of the process, device physics, and characterization teams in partnership with the PV Cell Engineering Lead, setting priorities that close real gaps to entitlement.

  • Scope and manage pilot line partnerships, and own the technology transfer strategy from pilot to production, including the make-vs-partner call.

  • Set cell procurement specs and drive supplier co-engineering while our own line comes up, so the cells we buy meet the same bar as the cells we intend to build.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 15+ years in silicon PV cell technology, with at least one cell architecture (TOPCon, HJT, or back-contact) taken from concept to production efficiency targets, and the roadmap behind it owned by you.

  • You've built and defended a full loss budget across recombination, optical, and resistive losses, and closed real gaps to entitlement on a shipping cell.

  • You've led process transfers from pilot to production and know firsthand what breaks, from tool matching to yield collapse.

  • You hold published or patented depth in passivation, contacts, or device design.

  • You've directed multi-disciplinary cell R&D teams spanning process, device physics, and characterization, and set their technical priorities.

  • You can commit to an efficiency and cost trajectory and defend it under pressure, to a CEO and a fab partner alike.

  • You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

  • Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

  • Bonus: SunPower/Maxeon, Fraunhofer ISE, ISC Konstanz, or UNSW lineage, FEOC-clean supply chain exposure, back-contact architecture depth, or pilot line buildout experience.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

The Product Engineering Team

Product Engineering takes the hardware behind gigawatt-scale AI data centers from concept to rate production: racks, gear, and power conversion built as products, not one-off projects.

Examples of key problems the team is working on:

  • Drive new product families (rack, gear, power conversion) through stage gates from kickoff to rate production on schedules set by data center delivery dates, not by when the design feels done.

  • Manage long-lead components and DVT-stage design changes against 20-week-plus lead times without blowing the program.

  • Keep design, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain converging on the same build, the same revision, and the same date across multiple concurrent programs.

  • Build gate reviews and readiness scoring rigorous enough that a pass means the product is actually ready, not that the meeting ran out of objections.

Role Scope

  • Own the program schedule, stage gates, and cross-functional execution for a product family (rack, gear, or power conversion) from kickoff through rate production.

  • Run risk and dependency management across design, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain, with tooling and judgment that surface the top risks early instead of a status-report factory that surfaces nothing.

  • Facilitate gate reviews and readiness scoring, and hold the line on what kills a pass, even when the schedule pressure says wave it through.

  • Broker escalations and decisions between engineering and delivery so long-lead calls get made in days instead of weeks.

  • Build program schedules that hold up even when the design team says everything is uncertain, with explicit assumptions and decision dates instead of padding.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 5-10 years of technical program management of hardware NPI at an OEM, ODM, or hyperscaler, running programs from kickoff through stage gates to rate production.

  • An engineering degree and enough technical depth to hold design reviews honest: you can tell the difference between a real answer and a slide.

  • You've made the hard call on a slipping program (cut scope, slip the date, or spend to recover) and can walk through the decision and what it cost.

  • You've handled a DVT-stage component change against a 20-week lead time and know how to run that decision: who's in the room, what data settles it, and how fast it has to close.

  • You build credible program schedules when the design team says everything is uncertain, and you know which uncertainties to force to a decision.

  • You track risk across 5+ workstreams with tooling and judgment instead of meetings, and the risks you flag are the ones that actually bite.

  • Bonus: GPU or dense compute hardware programs, switchgear or power conversion NPI, contract manufacturer management, or experience running ECO and change-discipline systems.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

The Product Engineering NPI Team

The NPI team takes hardware from design release to repeatable production across every product Fluidstack builds, from compute racks to medium-voltage switchgear.

Examples of key problems the team is working on:

  • Stand up a stage-gate NPI process that works across product families as different as rack-level compute integration and MV power equipment, without forcing them through the same checklist.

  • Run multiple concurrent NPI programs with a small TPM team, keeping schedule, readiness, and risk visible at the portfolio level.

  • Define what "ready to transfer" means with manufacturing engineering, so products land in production without a wave of post-transfer ECOs.

  • Enforce change discipline (ECOs, deviations, readiness criteria) at a pace that keeps up with the largest AI compute buildout in history.

Role Scope

  • Build the NPI process from scratch: gate definitions, readiness criteria, and ECO and change discipline that hold across products ranging from racks to MV switchgear.

  • Lead and develop the NPI TPM team, allocating 3 TPMs across 6 product families and making the tradeoffs explicit when coverage gets thin.

  • Own portfolio-level program visibility, with status and risk reporting rigorous enough that leadership hears about problems from you before anyone else.

  • Set the transfer-to-manufacturing standards with manufacturing engineering, defining exit criteria a program must clear before production takes ownership.

  • Hold the RACI between TPMs and engineering technical leads so ownership never blurs and no decision waits on a debate about whose call it is.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 10+ years in NPI or program management at a hardware OEM or ODM, with 3+ years leading TPM or NPI teams.

  • You've built stage-gate processes yourself, defining the gates, readiness criteria, and ECO discipline, not just operated inside a process someone else designed.

  • You've led TPM or NPI teams and developed the people in them, not just assigned their work.

  • You've managed programs spanning multiple product lines simultaneously and can show how you kept them all honest.

  • You've killed a program too late at least once, and you can name the signal you missed and what you watch for now.

  • You keep NPI lightweight enough that engineers use it instead of routing around it.

  • Bonus: portfolio management tooling, products spanning compute and power equipment, manufacturing transfer at new plants, or building teams from zero.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.
