The Legal Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Build the legal and compliance function from zero, for the largest compute buildout in history. No inherited playbook, no legacy team. The systems, standards, and team we build are the ones a company deploying gigawatts will run on for the next decade.

  • Make legal a source of speed. We structure and close complex deals in weeks that typically take quarters. That only work when we calibrate risk from first principles of business enablement. Our job is judgment, applied fast enough that legal helps drive the deal across the finish line.

  • Cover the entire legal surface with a lean team. A small team owns everything, and much of it involves business structures the market hasn’t seen before. You invent the solution with our business team.

Role Scope

  • Structure, draft, and negotiate the full range of real estate transactions behind Fluidstack’s data center buildout, including purchase and sale agreements, build-to-suit and ground leases, real estate financing, tax incentives, title review and insurance, zoning and land use, easements, environmental matters, and restrictive covenants.

  • Build the foundation for scale: create Fluidstack’s library of real estate form agreements and stand up the network of local counsel we need in each market.

  • Run complex negotiations with sophisticated counterparties end to end, balancing legal risk against the speed our business demands.

  • Manage outside counsel across substantive disciplines with rigor on scope, quality, and spend.

  • Quarterback transactions cross-functionally with site selection, development, finance, and delivery teams so deals never stall.

  • Advise business leaders as a strategic partner, anticipating legal and commercial issues before they arise and having solutions ready.

What We’re Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don’t fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You hold an active license to practice law in at least one jurisdiction and can meet admission requirements where you will practice.

  • You’ve autonomously structured, drafted, and negotiated complex commercial agreements as lead attorney, against sophisticated counterparties, with sophisticated practice in areas that map directly to data center real estate development: land acquisition and disposition, build-to-suit and ground leasing, real estate finance, zoning and land use, construction, title and insurance, and similar.

  • You’ve personally made sound, commercially pragmatic calls in ambiguous, high-stakes situations, and colleagues can point to deals where your judgment changed the outcome.

  • You’ve overseen outside counsel across multiple disciplines and held them to a rigorous bar on scope, quality, and spend.

  • You write and speak clearly enough to turn a dense legal issue into a decision and a next step for an executive or a counterparty.

  • Bonus: A mix of law firm and in-house experience. Using AI to improve legal work and efficiency. In-house experience at a data center developer or cloud company.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The HSE Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Own safety on gigawatts of high-energy infrastructure, built from zero. Headcount and sites are scaling faster than institutional knowledge can keep up. The gap between a control written on paper and one actually applied in the field is where fatalities happen.

  • Keep a 24/7 workforce running at full intensity, not sidelined by injury. Fatigue, shift work, and high-energy exposure compound on the people running the sites and show up as injuries or claims if no one is tracking them. The work is to catch them first.

  • Keep environmental compliance ahead of the fastest build in the industry. Behind-the-meter generation spans multiple states, each with its own air permit conditions, runtime limits, and reporting deadlines, and the company adds sites faster than any manual compliance model can keep up with.

Role Scope

  • Own hazardous energy control across multiple concurrent gigawatt-scale data center builds, from first temporary power through construction, Level 1 to Level 5 commissioning, and handoff to operations.

  • Write, review, and approve every switching plan, LOTO procedure, energization sequence, and zero-energy verification before medium-voltage or low-voltage gear is landed, tested, or turned on.

  • Run the pre-energization and energization kick-off meetings, and hold sole authority to authorize, pause, or stop any energization, isolation, or restoration across the GC, electrical contractors, commissioning agents, and the utility.

  • Audit the electrical safety program in the field: JHAs, energized work permits, boundary controls, PPE, arc flash labeling, and the gap between the written control and what the crew actually does at the gear.

  • Create and run the Kirk key program: collect, log, and control every Kirk key as switchgear, transformers, and generators are delivered to site, and turn the full key inventory over to operations at handoff.

  • Maintain the tamper seal program on all energized and isolated equipment, and act as the only person who can authorize breaking a tamper seal.

  • Manage the contract site-level Energy Marshals at every active campus: select and onboard them, set the standard they work to, audit their switching plans and field practice, and remove anyone who does not meet it.

  • Build the multi-site Energy Marshal standard, including the templates, energization tracker, and training, so a new campus stands up its energization program in days rather than months.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've performed as an Energy Marshal or Controlling Energy Marshal for a minimum of five years on data center or mission-critical construction, and have run energizations end to end on more than one site at a time.

  • You hold current NFPA 70E qualified-person training and a recognized electrical safety credential (NFPA CESCP or CESW), plus OSHA 30 Construction and current First Aid/CPR/AED.

  • You've personally written and approved switching orders and LOTO procedures on MV (above 1000V) and LV distribution: utility service, MV switchgear, transformers, generators, UPS, PDUs, and busway.

  • You've stopped an energization when the paperwork was signed but the field didn't match it, and you can walk through the call and how you got the work restarted safely.

  • You've directed other Energy Marshals or electrical safety leads across more than one site, held them to a single standard, and replaced one who fell short of it.

  • You've coordinated GC, electrical subcontractor, commissioning agent, utility, and owner operations teams on a live campus where construction and energized systems share walls.

  • You've run a Kirk key interlock or tamper seal program on live gear and can account for every key and seal from delivery through turnover.

  • You keep the energization log, permit records, and isolation registers current enough that an auditor or incident investigation can reconstruct any switching event on any site.

  • You explain arc flash boundaries, incident energy, and approach distances to an apprentice and to a VP with the same clarity.

  • Bonus: Electrician licensure (journeyman or master). Utility safety leadership (CUSP). Commissioning credentials (CxA, QCxP). Arc flash and coordination study review (SKM, ETAP). Behind-the-meter generation and multi-state utility interconnection.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Thermofluids R&D Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Reject 10s of GW of heat, starting now. Fluidstack is targeting 10s of GW of compute over the next two years. Every watt of it becomes heat that has to go somewhere, and no cooling team has ever been asked to open at that scale rather than grow into it.

  • Design and build the machines, because nobody can supply them. The merchant compressor market cannot deliver at this rate, and the vendor base behind today’s chillers will not scale to gigawatts. We are taking compressor and chiller design in house, working on machine architectures nobody sells today, and going from blank sheet to production faster than this industry thinks is possible.

  • Own every thermofluids problem behind the fleet, not just the chiller. Working fluid and cycle architecture, heat exchangers at a scale that dominates the cost of the plant, two-phase heat transfer at the chip, and thermal energy storage. All of it is open, and whatever this team lands gets built thousands of times.

Role Scope

  • Define what the machine has to be, owning the cycle model that sets the working fluid and the pressures, temperatures and flows the compressor, turbine and exchangers are designed against.

  • Design heat exchangers with surface areas running into millions of square meters, among the largest single drivers of a data center’s physical footprint.

  • Design the fluid system around the machine: piping, valves, headers, relief and isolation, sized against the pressure-drop budget the cycle can afford and the pressures the fluid actually runs at.

  • Run the trades that decide the machine: air-side temperature rise, face velocity and subcooling. Derive the operating points from coupled exchanger ratings rather than asserted approach temperatures, so infeasible designs get caught in the model instead of in hardware.

  • Take the cycle predictions onto the test stand and reconcile them against measured COP, then say plainly where the model was wrong.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 10+ years of experience in thermofluids engineering, including thermodynamic cycle modeling, heat exchanger design, and high-pressure fluid system design.

  • You’ve built a thermodynamic cycle model from fluid properties up and defended its assumptions to someone actively trying to break it.

  • You’ve sized real heat exchangers against published correlations, and you’ve caught a case where the correlation belonged to a different geometry than the one in front of you.

  • You’ve calibrated a model against a machine datasheet or test data and reported the gap honestly rather than tuning until it disappeared.

  • You’ve written the analysis that changed a design decision, in a form that people who never ran the code could read and act on.

  • You’ve sized a relief path and been the one who signed off that the system was protected.

  • You’ve held a result open when it was still open, instead of closing it early to be helpful.

  • You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

  • Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

  • Bonus: Vapor-compression and transcritical cycles (chillers, heat pumps, refrigeration). Propulsion and cryogenic fluid systems (feed systems, regenerative cooling, two-phase transport). Piping and relief design for high-pressure fluid systems. Real-gas properties and two-phase heat-transfer correlations (CoolProp, REFPROP, Cavallini, Gnielinski, Wang). Data center thermal architecture (CDUs, dry coolers, direct-to-chip).

All of it is open, and whatever this team lands gets built thousands of times.

Role Scope

  • Own the control architecture for the machine and the test rigs, spanning the compressor, the motor drive, the expansion turbine and the loop around them.

  • Write the safety interlocks and fault handling for a machine whose working fluid can cross its critical point inside the normal operating range, taking the control problem with it.

  • Deliver capacity control through motor and turbine speed rather than throttling valves, keeping the process fluid path free of valves at the design point.

  • Validate the control system against hardware-in-the-loop before it ever touches the real machine, and prove the interlocks fire.

  • Carry the controls out of the test cell and into the production chiller, including integration with site BMS and the wider plant.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 10+ years of experience in controls engineering for rotating machinery, including control architecture, safety interlocks, and hardware-in-the-loop validation.

  • You’ve written control logic for rotating machinery and you were in the room the first time it ran.

  • You’ve designed interlocks where a fault means destroyed hardware or an injured person, and you can justify every one of them from first principles.

  • You’ve run hardware-in-the-loop testing that caught something real before it reached commissioning.

  • You’ve tuned loops on a live machine and worked out why the model and the plant disagreed.

  • You’ve handed a control system to people who did not write it, with documentation they could actually use at three in the morning.

  • You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

  • Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

  • Bonus: Propulsion or vehicle test controls (engine sequencing, abort and safing logic). Variable-speed drives and high-speed motor control (VFDs, magnetic bearing controllers). Refrigeration and chiller control (superheat, head pressure, capacity staging). Industrial control platforms (Beckhoff, Siemens, Allen-Bradley, CODESYS). Model-based development and HIL (Simulink, dSPACE, NI VeriStand).

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Electrical Equipment Team

You'll join the product engineering group that designs the electrical equipment inside Fluidstack's data centers: medium-voltage switchgear, low-voltage switchboards and busway, and the prefabricated electrical skids and e-houses that carry them to site. We specify and design this equipment as products, not one-off procurements, so the same designs repeat across gigawatt-scale campuses and arrive on a schedule the build can hold.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Standardizing low-voltage switchboard and busway designs so a data hall's distribution can be ordered as a kit rather than engineered per site.

  • Sizing distribution for high-density compute loads whose power draw swings faster than conventional switchboard designs assume.

  • Qualifying busway and breaker sources across vendors while holding selective coordination and arc-flash limits.

  • Turning field and commissioning findings into design changes that reach the next production lot.

Role Scope

  • Own the low-voltage distribution product. Define the standard switchboard lineups, busway runs, tap-off units, and breaker schedules Fluidstack buys, and hold vendors to them.

  • Run the technical specification. Write and maintain the switchboard and busway specifications, including bus and breaker ratings, short-circuit withstand, metering and monitoring, and interfaces to UPS, transformers, and rack power.

  • Lead vendor engineering. Review vendor drawings, run factory acceptance tests, and close technical exceptions before release to manufacture.

  • Drive coordination and arc-flash. Deliver the low-voltage short-circuit, coordination, and arc-flash studies and set breaker settings the commissioning team can apply.

  • Design for the rack. Work with the rack systems team so busway, tap-offs, and rack power delivery are designed as one path from switchboard to server.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 15+ years of electrical engineering on low-voltage switchboards, switchgear, or busway, at an equipment manufacturer or specifying and commissioning it for data centers.

  • Hands-on with UL 891 switchboards, UL 1558 switchgear, UL 857 busway, and low-voltage power circuit breakers and their trip units.

  • You have run short-circuit, coordination, and arc-flash studies in ETAP, SKM, or equivalent and set trip units from them.

  • Working knowledge of NEC, NFPA 70E, and IEEE 1584 as they apply to data center distribution.

  • You have reviewed vendor submittals and run factory acceptance tests, and you know which exceptions matter.

  • You write specifications that a vendor can bid without a meeting.

  • You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

  • Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

  • Bonus: Professional Engineer license. Experience with high-density compute power distribution. Exposure to 800 V or other DC distribution schemes.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT TEAM

You'll join the product engineering group that designs the electrical equipment inside Fluidstack's data centers: medium-voltage switchgear, low-voltage switchboards and busway, and the prefabricated electrical skids and e-houses that carry them to site. We specify and design this equipment as products, not one-off procurements, so the same designs repeat across gigawatt-scale campuses and arrive on a schedule the build can hold.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - Moving electrical rooms off the critical path by building them as factory-tested skids and e-houses that ship with the switchgear already installed and wired.

 - Designing enclosures that hold switchgear ratings, arc-flash relief, cooling, and fire protection in outdoor installations across very different climates.

 - Qualifying skid and e-house fabricators and holding them to one drawing set across repeat orders.

 - Turning field and commissioning findings into design changes that reach the next production lot.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own the electrical skid and e-house product. Define the standard enclosure families, layouts, and equipment fit-outs Fluidstack buys, and hold fabricators to them.

 - Run the technical specification. Write and maintain the skid and e-house specifications, covering structure, enclosure ratings, HVAC and pressurization, arc-flash relief, grounding, cable entry, fire detection and suppression, and the interfaces to switchgear, transformers, and site civil work.

 - Lead fabricator engineering. Review fabricator drawings, run factory acceptance and integrated tests before shipment, and close technical exceptions before release.

 - Integrate the equipment. Coordinate with the switchgear, switchboard, and controls engineers so each e-house ships as a tested system, not a shell with parts inside.

 - Deliver to site. Set the shipping, rigging, setting, and site-connection requirements so an e-house energizes on the construction schedule.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

 - 15+ years of electrical engineering on prefabricated electrical skids, e-houses, or power control rooms, at a fabricator or specifying and commissioning them for industrial or mission-critical facilities.

 - Hands-on with medium- and low-voltage switchgear installation inside enclosures, including arc-flash venting, clearances, cable management, and grounding.

 - You have delivered at least one e-house program from specification through factory test and site energization.

 - Working knowledge of NEC, IEEE C37.20, NFPA 70E, and the structural and HVAC requirements for outdoor electrical enclosures.

 - You have reviewed fabricator submittals and run factory acceptance tests, and you know which exceptions matter.

 - You write specifications that a fabricator can bid without a meeting.

 - You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

 - Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

 - Bonus: Professional Engineer license. Modular construction or factory-built infrastructure experience. Exposure to skids for high-density compute loads.



We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Electrical Equipment Team

You'll join the product engineering group that designs the electrical equipment inside Fluidstack's data centers: medium-voltage switchgear, low-voltage switchboards and busway, and the prefabricated electrical skids and e-houses that carry them to site. We specify and design this equipment as products, not one-off procurements, so the same designs repeat across gigawatt-scale campuses and arrive on a schedule the build can hold.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Standardizing medium-voltage switchgear lineups so that long-lead orders can be placed before a site's final electrical design is complete.

  • Qualifying second and third sources for switchgear, breakers, and protection relays without reopening the design each time.

  • Holding arc-flash, short-circuit, and coordination margins across equipment from different vendors.

  • Turning field and commissioning findings into design changes that reach the next production lot.

Role Scope

  • Own the medium-voltage switchgear product. Define the standard lineups, ratings, and configurations Fluidstack buys, and hold vendors to them.

  • Run the technical specification. Write and maintain the switchgear specifications, including bus ratings, breaker duty, protection and metering, arc-resistant construction, and interface requirements to transformers and e-houses.

  • Lead vendor engineering. Review vendor drawings, run factory acceptance tests, and close technical exceptions before release to manufacture.

  • Drive protection coordination. Deliver the short-circuit and coordination studies for the medium-voltage system and set relay settings the commissioning team can apply.

  • Feed the roadmap. Bring emerging switchgear technology, including solid-state and higher-voltage options, into the product roadmap with cost and schedule cases.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 15+ years of electrical engineering on medium-voltage switchgear, either at an equipment manufacturer or specifying and commissioning it for mission-critical facilities.

  • Hands-on with metal-clad and metal-enclosed switchgear, vacuum circuit breakers, protection relays, and arc-resistant designs.

  • You have run short-circuit, arc-flash, and coordination studies in ETAP, SKM, or equivalent and set relays from them.

  • Working knowledge of IEEE C37, IEC 62271, and NEC requirements for medium-voltage installations.

  • You have reviewed vendor submittals and run factory acceptance tests, and you know which exceptions matter.

  • You write specifications that a vendor can bid without a meeting.

  • You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

  • Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

  • Bonus: Professional Engineer license. Experience with switchgear for high-density compute loads. Exposure to solid-state breakers or medium-voltage DC.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.


Applicant Privacy Notice
AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The HSE Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Build the sustainability program for one of the largest compute buildouts in history, from zero. The first GHG inventory, the first disclosures, the first water strategy, all written here while the company adds gigawatts.

  • Make our carbon and water numbers hold up to the most demanding audience in tech. Hyperscaler customers, auditors, and regulators will test every figure, so the accounting gets built right the first time.

  • Keep environmental compliance ahead of the fastest build in the industry. Behind-the-meter generation spans multiple states, each with its own air permit conditions, runtime limits, and reporting deadlines, and the company adds sites faster than any manual compliance model can keep up with.

Role Scope

  • Own the workers compensation program across every business unit: data center operations, construction, manufacturing, and corporate, from carrier and TPA selection through claim reserves, reviews, and closure.

  • Run case management for every work-related injury and illness end to end, from first report through treatment, fitness-for-duty, and full-duty return, with an occupational medicine and clinic network stood up in each state we operate in.

  • Build the return-to-work program so injured employees are back on modified or full duty in days, with transitional duty defined ahead of time for shift-based field roles.

  • Stand up the industrial hygiene and ergonomics programs for high-energy sites and the manufacturing facility: exposure assessments, sampling, heat, noise, and fatigue controls, ergonomic risk reduction for shift-based field work, and medical surveillance where exposures require it.

  • Own injury and illness recordkeeping across all sites so OSHA 300, 300A, and 301 logs, electronic submissions, and state filings are accurate, current, and defensible on inspection.

  • Turn claims, near-miss, and clinic data into a single view of injury trends and cost drivers that leadership and site HSE teams act on before the next claim, not after.

What We’re Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don’t fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You’ve personally managed a multi-state workers compensation program for a workforce of thousands, including carrier and TPA relationships, reserve reviews, and premium and experience-mod outcomes you can point to.

  • You’ve run case management for high-severity injuries in construction, manufacturing, or heavy industry, and your former employer’s return-to-work numbers moved because of you.

  • You’ve built a return-to-work or transitional duty program from nothing and gotten field supervisors and union or contractor workforces to use it.

  • You’ve led industrial hygiene and ergonomics work in the field: written the exposure assessments, pulled the samples, redesigned a task that was producing injuries, and stood up medical surveillance for a real hazard.

  • You’ve owned OSHA recordkeeping across many sites and been through an inspection or audit where the logs held up.

  • You work directly with carriers, adjusters, defense counsel, occupational physicians, HR on leave and accommodation interplay, and injured employees in the same week, and each of them gets a clear answer and a next step from you.

  • You build the program from data: you’ve pulled claims and clinic data into a trend view a COO would read and changed a control because of what it showed.

  • Bonus: Industrial hygiene or safety credentials (CIH, CSP). Case management or disability management credentials (CCM, CPDM, occupational health RN). Self-insured or high-deductible workers compensation programs and captive structures. Multi-state compliance in the states where we build (Texas non-subscriber rules, New York, Indiana, Louisiana). Claims and injury analytics tooling (Origami, Riskonnect, Intelex).

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.


Applicant Privacy Notice
AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

The People Team

  • Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Building the people function from scratch, fast enough to keep up with 10x growth, including the immigration and mobility programs a global, fast-hiring company needs.

  • Reinventing people operations around AI so a small team supports many times its number.

  • Owning the culture and comms as the company scales across sites and countries.

Role Scope

  • Serve as the people partner for your client orgs, the first call for managers on hiring, performance, structure, and the hard conversations.

  • Own Fluidstack's immigration and visa sponsorship program, from case strategy through filing coordination with outside counsel, for both new hires and existing employees.

  • Own employee relations end to end: investigate, resolve, and document with judgment and speed.

  • Run the people rhythms for your groups: onboarding, reviews, engagement, and offboarding that scale with 10x growth.

  • Coach managers, many of them first-time, into leaders their teams would choose again.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

  • You've owned an employer-sponsored immigration program directly, including H-1B, O-1, L-1, or PERM cases, and know the process well enough to manage outside counsel rather than just route to them.

  • You've been an HRBP or people partner through rapid scaling, and your client leaders would hire you again.

  • You've run sensitive ER cases end to end and your investigations held up.

  • Vendor/broker management. Source, evaluate, and negotiate with insurance brokers and carriers; run renewal RFPs to ensure competitive pricing and coverage terms as the portfolio grows.

  • Premium and budget management. Own the insurance budget, forecast premium spend as new sites and assets come online, and manage the renewal cycle across property, casualty, and builder's risk lines.

  • Compliance and requirements tracking. Ensure coverage meets contractual requirements from lenders, JV partners, customers, and landlords (minimum limits, additional insured status, certificates of insurance), and keep documentation audit-ready.

Role Scope

  • Own every insurance program at Fluidstack end to end, from program design and broker selection through placement, renewal, and budget, across property, construction, liability, and cargo lines.

  • Run claims from first notice to resolution, driving brokers, TPAs, carriers, and Legal to outcomes instead of waiting on them.

  • Drive loss control and property risk engineering across operating sites and active gigawatt-scale construction, turning risk engineering recommendations into completed fixes with Construction, HSE, and Data Center Operations.

  • Gather and analyze exposure data across a fleet growing by gigawatts and land complete, on-time renewal submissions to underwriters every cycle.

  • Set the insurance requirements in leases, EPC contracts, and vendor and customer agreements, and review counterparty terms so coverage gaps never surface mid-claim.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've managed commercial property and casualty insurance programs yourself, on the corporate risk management or brokerage side, and you know how property, construction, and liability lines actually get structured, placed, and priced.

  • You've run claims to resolution, including large or contested ones, coordinating litigation counsel, TPAs, adjusters, and carriers on strategy rather than just processing paperwork.

  • You've worked property risk engineering in the field: walking sites, pushing loss control recommendations through the people who own the fix, and knowing what underwriters will flag before they do.

  • You've built renewal submissions under hard deadlines with high-volume, messy exposure data pulled from stakeholders who had other priorities.

  • You read contracts for insurance terms and catch the gap between what an agreement requires and what a policy actually covers.

  • You explain insurance to engineers, lawyers, and executives clearly enough that they act on it.

  • Bonus: Insurance designations (CPCU, ARM). Capital-intensive or construction-heavy industries (data centers, energy, semiconductors). Construction insurance programs (builder's risk, OCIP/CCIP). High-value equipment in transit (cargo, stock throughput).

The Supply Chain Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Supply tens of gigawatts of compute, the largest build out of compute in history. Qualify and multi-source across every critical equipment category, with lead-time and capacity thresholds tied directly to the forward build pipeline.

  • Make supply chain the reason we build faster than anyone. Our modular build redefines speed in this industry, and it lives or dies on supply chain. Keep procurement permanently off the critical path so schedule compression stays our advantage, not our constraint.

  • Build the most accurate supply chain prediction modelling that exists. Use the frontier of AI to forecast lead times, demand, and disruption with a precision the industry has never had, and turn that foresight into a structural edge.

Role Scope

  • Own sourcing and buying for every critical equipment category behind a tens of gigawatts build: switchgear, transformers, generators, UPS, chillers, CDUs, and the long-lead gear that sets the schedule.

  • Lock vendor capacity and lead times against the forward build pipeline.

  • Hold vendors to their production ramps by tracking every commitment from PO to delivery and acting the day a ship date slips.

  • Build the category team: hire category leads and buyers, define the sourcing playbook, and own the results.

  • Work with Design, Construction, and Manufacturing so equipment lands before the schedule needs it and procurement never sits on the critical path.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've personally owned nine-figure direct materials spend on physical equipment, and you can walk through the numbers from memory.

  • You've held vendors to production ramp commitments, and you can name the time a supplier slipped and what you did that week.

  • You've built a category or sourcing team: hired the people, set the process, and handed off categories that kept delivering.

  • You've worked electrical and mechanical equipment lead times hands-on, down to the factory slot and the test date.

  • You've scaled supply at a company going from prototype to volume, where the playbook didn't exist and you wrote it.

  • You've made sourcing calls on incomplete data, owned the ones that went wrong, and can say what you changed after.

  • Bonus: Data center or utility-scale electrical equipment. Fast-scaling hardware: EV, aerospace, energy storage. Dual-sourcing a critical category through a supply shock. Supplier quality and factory acceptance testing programs. Modular or offsite construction supply chains.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Civil, Structural and Architectural Team

You'll join the civil, structural, and architectural engineers who design the buildings, sites, and yards for Fluidstack's gigawatt-scale AI data centers. The team works from template designs that repeat across campuses, and every template carries large mechanical plant, on-site generation, and electrical yards whose sound has to be understood before the first site is permitted. This role is the team's acoustics specialist and the point of contact for noise across the data center and power generation engineering groups.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Predicting property-line and community noise from template data center designs with hundreds of fans, chillers, and dry coolers running at full load, before a site is chosen.

  • Quantifying the noise of on-site gas generation, transformers, and switchyards and folding it into the same site model.

  • Choosing mitigations that work as repeatable products, such as barriers, silencers, enclosures, and equipment selection, rather than site-by-site fixes.

  • Keeping occupied work areas inside and around the plant within occupational noise limits as equipment density rises.

Role Scope

  • Own the acoustic studies. Run environmental and occupational noise studies and calculations for the template data center and power generation designs, and keep them current as the templates change.

  • Model the sites. Build and maintain outdoor sound propagation models for each template and adapt them to candidate sites, terrain, and local ordinances.

  • Recommend the mitigations. Specify barriers, silencers, acoustic enclosures, louvers, and equipment selections that bring sites within limits, with the cost and schedule case for each.

  • Work across engineering. Bring noise requirements into the mechanical, electrical, power generation, and architectural designs early, and review their equipment selections and layouts for acoustic impact.

  • Protect the workforce. Set occupational noise exposure limits for plant and yard work areas, define hearing conservation zones, and verify them at commissioning.

  • Support permitting. Produce the noise assessments, reports, and measurements that permitting and community engagement need, and answer the questions that come back.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 5+ years of acoustics or noise control engineering on industrial, power generation, or mission-critical facilities, with at least one project taken from study through permit and commissioning measurement.

  • Fluency in an outdoor sound propagation tool such as CadnaA or SoundPLAN and in the ISO 9613-2 method behind it.

  • Hands-on with environmental noise measurement, sound power and sound pressure data from equipment vendors, and octave-band calculations.

  • Working knowledge of occupational noise standards such as OSHA 1910.95 and the local noise ordinances that govern industrial sites.

  • You have specified barriers, silencers, and acoustic enclosures and seen them built and measured.

  • You explain acoustic trade-offs to mechanical and electrical engineers in their terms and hold the line on limits when a design review wants to spend them.

  • Bonus: INCE Board Certification or Professional Engineer license. Data center or gas turbine plant noise experience. Building acoustics or vibration isolation background. Mechanical engineering or procurement experience.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

 - Predicting property-line and community noise from template data center designs with hundreds of fans, chillers, and dry coolers running at full load, before a site is chosen.

 - Quantifying the noise of on-site gas generation, transformers, and switchyards and folding it into the same site model.

 - Choosing mitigations that work as repeatable products, such as barriers, silencers, enclosures, and equipment selection, rather than site-by-site fixes.

 - Keeping occupied work areas inside and around the plant within occupational noise limits as equipment density rises.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own the acoustic studies. Run environmental and occupational noise studies and calculations for the template data center and power generation designs, and keep them current as the templates change.

 - Model the sites. Build and maintain outdoor sound propagation models for each template and adapt them to candidate sites, terrain, and local ordinances.

 - Recommend the mitigations. Specify barriers, silencers, acoustic enclosures, louvers, and equipment selections that bring sites within limits, with the cost and schedule case for each.

 - Work across engineering. Bring noise requirements into the mechanical, electrical, power generation, and architectural designs early, and review their equipment selections and layouts for acoustic impact.

 - Protect the workforce. Set occupational noise exposure limits for plant and yard work areas, define hearing conservation zones, and verify them at commissioning.

 - Support permitting. Produce the noise assessments, reports, and measurements that permitting and community engagement need, and answer the questions that come back.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

 - 5+ years of acoustics or noise control engineering on industrial, power generation, or mission-critical facilities, with at least one project taken from study through permit and commissioning measurement.

 - Fluency in an outdoor sound propagation tool such as CadnaA or SoundPLAN and in the ISO 9613-2 method behind it.

 - Hands-on with environmental noise measurement, sound power and sound pressure data from equipment vendors, and octave-band calculations.

 - Working knowledge of occupational noise standards such as OSHA 1910.95 and the local noise ordinances that govern industrial sites.

 - You have specified barriers, silencers, and acoustic enclosures and seen them built and measured.

 - You explain acoustic trade-offs to mechanical and electrical engineers in their terms and hold the line on limits when a design review wants to spend them.

 - Bonus: INCE Board Certification or Professional Engineer license. Data center or gas turbine plant noise experience. Building acoustics or vibration isolation background. Mechanical engineering or procurement experience.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • You've caught a struggling site early and fixed it before it slipped a build or shipment schedule.

  • You write clearly enough to turn a fleet-wide production issue into a decision a CEO or COO can make in one read.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Engineering Program Management Team

You'll join the technical program managers who run Fluidstack's infrastructure R&D programs. This role sits with the Electrical Equipment product engineering group, which is designing the medium-voltage switchgear, low-voltage switchboards and busway, and prefabricated electrical skids and e-houses that Fluidstack will manufacture in its own factory rather than buy from the market. Your job is to drive those designs from concept to a released, manufacturable product on a schedule the factory and the build can hold.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Taking equipment that the industry buys as catalog products and re-engineering it as Fluidstack-owned designs with a bill of materials, drawings, and test procedures a factory line can build to.

  • Running concept, preliminary, and critical design reviews across several equipment families in parallel and closing the actions they generate.

  • Qualifying the components and sub-suppliers each design depends on, with second sources, before the design is frozen.

  • Handing a released design to manufacturing engineering with the documentation, tooling, and test plan needed for the first production lot.

Role Scope

  • Drive the design program. Own the integrated plan for one or more electrical equipment product lines from requirements through design release, and hold the engineering team to its gates.

  • Run the design reviews. Schedule and run concept, preliminary, and critical design reviews, capture decisions and actions, and close them before the next gate.

  • Make it manufacturable. Bring manufacturing engineering, quality, and supply chain into the design early so bills of materials, tolerances, and test procedures are ready when the design releases.

  • Manage the component supply. Track long-lead components, sub-supplier qualification, and second sourcing against the design schedule, and escalate what will slip.

  • Hold the configuration. Keep specifications, drawings, and change requests in one controlled set so the factory builds what engineering released.

  • Report the truth. Keep program status, risks, and spend visible to engineering leadership without waiting to be asked.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 5+ years of technical program management on electrical or electromechanical hardware that was designed and manufactured in house, ideally switchgear, switchboards, power distribution, or electrical enclosures.

  • You have taken at least one hardware product from concept through design release and first production lot, running the design review gates along the way.

  • You understand design for manufacturing, configuration management, and how a bill of materials, drawing package, and test procedure get a design onto a factory line.

  • You read electrical single-lines, equipment schedules, and mechanical drawings well enough to catch a problem before the engineer does.

  • You have managed component suppliers and sub-supplier qualification to a design schedule.

  • You write clear, short status that an executive can act on and an engineer will not dispute.

  • Bonus: Electrical engineering degree or PE license. UL 891, UL 1558, or IEEE C37 product certification experience. New product introduction in a low-volume, high-mix factory.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

The Decision Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Automate the delivery of gigawatts. Every process that takes AI infrastructure from land to live compute becomes software: schedules, decisions, and todos generated from a live knowledge graph instead of chased by hand.

  • Forward-deploy beside the experts. Product teams sit with quality managers, sourcing leads, and deployment engineers on factory floors and sites, and turn their judgment into systems that reach every unit.

  • Deliver every supercomputer faster than the last. Dozens of concurrent projects feed one graph, so every lesson learned at one site becomes a preventive check at all of them.

Role Scope

  • Build the hiring machine as software. Hiring is the company's biggest bottleneck. Every role, seat, and interview loop already lives in one graph, and you take it the rest of the way: the recruiting system synced both directions, interviewer supply and load visible to every hiring manager, and onboarding generated the moment an offer is signed, so day one starts with the job instead of the checklist.

  • Build the cash view the company runs on: today no system derives near term spend, so finance forecasts by hand and misses what construction already committed. You turn purchase orders, contract terms, and build milestones into an order schedule, a cash demand curve by month, and a payment schedule that recompute as procurement and construction move.

  • Build one capital pipeline from approved budget to released capital to spent dollar, gated on build milestones the delivery system already verifies, with the proof chain behind every financing drawdown assembled automatically, so releasing nine figures takes a day of judgment and funding follows construction within days.

  • Parse every MSA, change order, and side letter into obligations, prices, deadlines, penalties, and SLAs, so a delivery lead gets what we owe a customer at a site with the clause attached, a change order arrives with its legal and finance checks done, and the corpus of executed deals prices the next negotiation.

  • Embed forward-deployed with finance, treasury, accounting, legal, and people teams through a close, a drawdown, a negotiation, and a hiring loop, and turn their approvals, contract terms, screens, and reconciliations into structured data and generated work, including a continuous close where capitalization and depreciation post as events the moment they happen.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've shipped production code in Go, Python, or TypeScript, and you pick up whatever language the problem demands.

  • You've built real features on LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, or open-weight models), MCP servers, and agentic frameworks.

  • You work daily with AI coding tools like Claude Code and Cursor, and you get agents doing useful work autonomously alongside you.

  • You identify problems, design the solution, and ship it without waiting for direction or approval.

  • You've moved fast under deadline while leaving foundations that other engineers extended after you moved on.

  • You've earned credibility with experts outside engineering: finance leads, lawyers, recruiters, or auditors, and driven adoption of your software inside their real deadlines, like a working close calendar or an offer that has to go out today.

  • Your product taste shows in what you've shipped: a controller, a recruiter, or a lawyer calls your interface obvious, and the workflow matches how their work actually happens.

  • Bonus: ERP and fixed asset accounting. FP&A, cash forecasting, and capital planning. Structured finance or treasury operations. Contract lifecycle systems. ATS and HRIS integrations (Ashby, Greenhouse, Rippling, Workday). LLM extraction over legal and financial documents.

Benefits:

  • Competitive total compensation package (cash + equity)

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Retirement plan

  • Generous PTO policy

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Mechanical Engineering Team

You'll join the mechanical engineers in Fluidstack's infrastructure R&D group, who design the cooling, water, and fire systems inside gigawatt-scale AI data centers as repeatable products rather than one-off site designs. Liquid-cooled compute makes water a primary utility: make-up water, treatment, condenser and process loops, and drainage all have to be sized, specified, and standardized so the same design ships to every site.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Standardizing the domestic, process, and make-up water systems that feed liquid cooling plants so they can be ordered as kits and installed in prefabricated modules.

  • Sizing water supply, storage, and drainage for cooling loads that swing faster than conventional plumbing design assumes.

  • Coordinating water treatment, backflow protection, and chemical dosing with the controls and water-quality engineers who operate the loops.

  • Turning field and commissioning findings into design changes that reach the next site.

Role Scope

  • Own the plumbing design. Design domestic water, process and make-up water, condenser water piping, drainage, and stormwater systems for data center buildings and prefabricated modules, from concept through construction documents.

  • Size and specify. Run hydraulic calculations, select pumps, valves, backflow preventers, water heaters, and storage, and write the specifications vendors and contractors build to.

  • Hold the codes. Keep designs compliant with plumbing, mechanical, and health codes across the jurisdictions Fluidstack builds in, and manage the permit and inspection questions that come back.

  • Integrate with cooling. Work with the mechanical, water-quality, and controls engineers so make-up water, treatment, and blowdown are designed as one system with the cooling plant.

  • Support the build. Review contractor submittals and shop drawings, answer RFIs, and walk installations through commissioning.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 5+ years of plumbing or piping design engineering on industrial, mission-critical, or large commercial facilities, with at least one project taken through construction documents and commissioning.

  • Working knowledge of the IPC or UPC, IMC, and local amendments, and of how to get a design through permit review.

  • Hands-on with hydraulic calculations, pump and pipe sizing, backflow protection, and water storage design.

  • Fluency in Revit or AutoCAD MEP and a hydraulic modeling tool.

  • You have reviewed contractor submittals and answered RFIs, and you know which deviations matter.

  • You write specifications a contractor can bid without a meeting.

  • Bonus: Professional Engineer license or CPD certification. Data center or liquid-cooling plant experience. Water treatment or industrial process piping background.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

Role Scope

  • Build the fleet health system: real-time telemetry and tiered healthchecks on every machine across Kubernetes and bare metal, rolled into one API the whole company trusts to answer "is this machine healthy," with alarms correlated into incidents that reach on-call with a drafted probable cause.

  • Turn repair and RMA into generated work: one tracked flow from failure detection through triage, parts, vendor return, and return to service, where failure thresholds route machines to repair automatically, each production engineer's shift todo list is generated for them, and time to return to service is a number the system reports.

  • Ship hardware qualification as software: burn-in, performance baselining, and new hardware validation composed into rack-level workflows, so bringing thousands of accelerators online is a repeatable run and every machine enters production with its acceptance evidence attached in the graph.

  • Run the facility on the same system as the fleet: the maintenance system for lockout tagout and work orders is live at one site and rolls out to two more, every asset register loads before the first external audit this fall, and the legacy datacenter inventory retires before the next building energizes. You own the asset model, the migration, and the day the old tools switch off.

  • Turn every runbook into a checked procedure: SOPs, training records, and technician qualifications become structured data the customer can audit, and site SLOs, deployment cycle time, and labor ramp report themselves on the dashboards a hyperscaler customer asked for. You work forward-deployed beside production engineers and facility operators, on site and on the rotation, and build what they use the next shift.

  • You've moved fast under deadline while leaving foundations that other engineers extended after you moved on.

  • You've sat the on-call rotation or worked beside the people who do, and you've turned operational pain into systems that made the pager quieter.

  • Your product taste shows in what you've shipped: interfaces the engineers on the rotation call obvious, and workflows that match how the work actually happens.

  • Bonus: Production engineering or SRE on large GPU fleets. Hardware qualification or burn-in frameworks. BMC, Redfish, or IPMI tooling. CMMS, DCIM, or asset management systems. BMS/EPMS or SCADA. Prometheus and Grafana.

  • Competitive total compensation package (cash + equity)

  • Generous PTO policy

  • Close the loop from receiving to payment: every delivery matches a purchase order line, every warehouse bin knows its serial numbers, cycle counts are scored against an accuracy gate, and finance three-way matches from the same record, so the question "did we get what we paid for" has one answer instead of three.

  • Ship manufacturing as software before the factory opens: manufacturing bills of materials, engineering change notices, and the drawing tree live in one model, inspection and test plans and first article procedures generate per asset from the design revision, and a failed check opens a nonconformance with the evidence attached and rescores the vendor.

  • Embed with sourcing leads, quality managers, factory operators, and warehouse teams, on their floors and in their vendor calls, and turn their judgment into the systems that decide the order schedule, the cash demand by month, and the payment schedule the company plans against.

  • You've earned credibility with operators in factories, warehouses, or procurement, and driven adoption of your software inside their real deadlines, like a live production run or a quarter-end close.

  • Your product taste shows in what you've shipped: interfaces the floor calls obvious, and workflows that match how the work actually happens.

  • Bonus: MES, ERP, WMS, or TMS systems. BOM lineage, engineering change control, and serialized component traceability. Supplier quality (NCRs, CAPA, FAI). Three-way match and receiving reconciliation. LLM extraction over vendor documents. High-volume hardware supply chains.

Benefits:

  • Competitive total compensation package (cash + equity)

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Retirement plan

  • Generous PTO policy

Role Scope

  • Build the schedule that runs the portfolio: one template schedule per building type, instantiated per project, with every activity tied to the materials it consumes, so need-by dates for switchgear, transformers, and cooling fall out of the critical path instead of a spreadsheet, and a slip in permitting reprices the procurement calendar the same hour.

  • Turn the site into structured data: work packages, contractor field entries, rack placements, cable runs, and QA inspections land as records tied to the design revision they were built against, percent complete is computed from evidence rather than reported on a call, and the customer sees delivered against committed without anyone assembling a deck.

  • Ship change orders as a workflow, not an email chain: scope, cost, and schedule impact drafted from the design delta, routed through legal, finance, and the general contractor with the approval trail attached, and the bill of materials and schedule updated the moment the order is signed.

  • Make the design the source of truth: ingest building information models straight into the bill of materials with a reviewable diff on every revision, generate submittal requirements per spec section, and keep sites, buildings, and data halls as one canonical record that every downstream system reads instead of copies.

  • Ship commissioning as software: test procedures generated per asset from the design revision across all five levels, results landing as evidence against the asset they tested, energization gates that check themselves, and handover that opens on proof instead of a signature.

  • Your product taste shows in what you've shipped: interfaces field crews call obvious, and workflows that match how the work actually happens.

  • Bonus: Construction tech or project controls (P6, schedule engines, critical path). BIM, IFC, or Revit data models. Commissioning, BMS/EPMS, or controls protocols. Document control and submittal workflows. Graph data models. Computer vision on site imagery.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Retirement plan

  • Generous PTO policy
