About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The People Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Build the people function from scratch, fast enough to keep up with 10x growth. You'll build the systems, programs, and team from nothing, and make them work before we outgrow them.

  • Reinvent people operations around AI. Doing this by hand doesn't scale to a workforce growing this fast on a team this lean. You'll put AI at the core of how the function runs, so a small team supports many times its number.

  • Shape the culture and comms as the company scales. When a company scales this quickly, staying connected and aligned doesn't happen on its own. You'll help shape internal comms, events, and rhythm that keep a multi-site team that's growing fast bound to a shared culture.

Role Scope

  • Own Fluidstack's benefits program end to end, covering medical, dental, vision, life and AD&D, disability, EAP, FSA, HSA, HRA, commuter, voluntary benefits, and the 401(k) with Fidelity, and decide which new benefits (fertility, family-building, mental health) we add next.

  • Run annual renewal and open enrollment start to finish: model claims, cost trends, and contribution options with Finance, benchmark against AI and technology peers, bring recommendations to leadership well before enrollment, and audit every election across HRIS, payroll, and carrier systems afterward.

  • Keep every plan compliant as we expand into new states and entities, covering ERISA, ACA reporting (1094-C and 1095-C), COBRA, HIPAA, FMLA, Section 125, plan documents and required notices, state paid leave laws, and audit readiness.

  • Run benefits operations in our HRIS and carrier feeds so eligibility, deductions, and life events stay accurate every pay cycle, and hold brokers, carriers, and TPAs to their service levels through renewals, RFPs, and implementations.

  • Administer leave and accommodations (FMLA, state paid leave, disability, parental, and military leave) with carriers, Payroll, HR Business Partners, and Legal, and serve as the go-to expert when an employee's benefits question is complex, urgent, or personal.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've owned a US benefits program end to end, from broker and carrier renewal through open enrollment and the post-enrollment audit of every election.

  • You've personally handled benefits compliance (ERISA, ACA reporting and affordability testing, COBRA, HIPAA, FMLA, Section 125) and you know exactly where your knowledge ends and benefits counsel begins.

  • You've administered leave and accommodations across multiple states and kept the company compliant as state laws changed underneath you.

  • You've been the primary admin of an HRIS and benefits platform (Rippling), including eligibility rules and carrier EDI feeds, and you reconcile HRIS, payroll, and carrier data in spreadsheets yourself.

  • You've built benefits cost and utilization reporting, modeled renewal and contribution scenarios with Finance, and driven leadership to a decision on cost versus coverage.

  • You write benefits guides and run education sessions employees actually act on, and you can point to the drop in tickets or enrollment errors that followed.

  • You handle confidential health and personal data with discretion, and you build checks so a missed enrollment or payroll error never happens twice.

  • Bonus: Benefits certifications (CEBS, CBP). Hypergrowth benefits builds (headcount doubling or more in a year, new states and entities). International benefits (UK, employer of record). Benefits diligence and integration for acquisitions. AI tools for benefits administration and employee support (chat-based benefits assistants).

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.


Applicant Privacy Notice
AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Decision Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Automate the delivery of gigawatts. Every process that takes AI infrastructure from land to live compute becomes software: schedules, decisions, and todos generated from a live knowledge graph instead of chased by hand.

  • Forward-deploy beside the experts. Product teams sit with quality managers, sourcing leads, and deployment engineers on factory floors and sites, and turn their judgment into systems that reach every unit.

  • Deliver every supercomputer faster than the last. Dozens of concurrent projects feed one graph, so every lesson learned at one site becomes a preventive check at all of them.

Role Scope

  • Build the fleet health system: real-time telemetry and tiered healthchecks on every machine across Kubernetes and bare metal, rolled into one API the whole company trusts to answer "is this machine healthy," with alarms correlated into incidents that reach on-call with a drafted probable cause.

  • Turn repair and RMA into generated work: one tracked flow from failure detection through triage, parts, vendor return, and return to service, where failure thresholds route machines to repair automatically, each production engineer's shift todo list is generated for them, and time to return to service is a number the system reports.

  • Ship hardware qualification as software: burn-in, performance baselining, and new hardware validation composed into rack-level workflows, so bringing thousands of accelerators online is a repeatable run and every machine enters production with its acceptance evidence attached in the graph.

  • Run the facility on the same system as the fleet: the maintenance system for lockout tagout and work orders is live at one site and rolls out to two more, every asset register loads before the first external audit this fall, and the legacy datacenter inventory retires before the next building energizes. You own the asset model, the migration, and the day the old tools switch off.

  • Turn every runbook into a checked procedure: SOPs, training records, and technician qualifications become structured data the customer can audit, and site SLOs, deployment cycle time, and labor ramp report themselves on the dashboards a hyperscaler customer asked for. You work forward-deployed beside production engineers and facility operators, on site and on the rotation, and build what they use the next shift.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've shipped production code in Go, Python, or TypeScript, and you pick up whatever language the problem demands.

  • You've built real features on LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, or open-weight models), MCP servers, and agentic frameworks.

  • You work daily with AI coding tools like Claude Code and Cursor, and you get agents doing useful work autonomously alongside you.

  • You identify problems, design the solution, and ship it without waiting for direction or approval.

  • You've moved fast under deadline while leaving foundations that other engineers extended after you moved on.

  • You've sat the on-call rotation or worked beside the people who do, and you've turned operational pain into systems that made the pager quieter.

  • Your product taste shows in what you've shipped: interfaces the engineers on the rotation call obvious, and workflows that match how the work actually happens.

  • Bonus: Production engineering or SRE on large GPU fleets. Hardware qualification or burn-in frameworks. BMC, Redfish, or IPMI tooling. CMMS, DCIM, or asset management systems. BMS/EPMS or SCADA. Prometheus and Grafana.

    Benefits:

  • Competitive total compensation package (cash + equity)

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Retirement plan

  • Generous PTO policy

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.


Applicant Privacy Notice
AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

Role Scope

  • Turn the bill of materials into the order book: every template bill carries the price and lead time of each line, every project bill locks against a building, and every purchase order derives from it, so tens of billions of dollars of GPUs, optics, switchgear, and cooling are ordered from one source of truth instead of a spreadsheet.

  • Make procurement tracking trustworthy: the rules that decide when a line is late, what its status means, and which lines sit on the critical path run in code against live vendor emails, documents, and general contractor purchase orders through the extractors you ship, so drift is caught the week it happens and the recovery plan is drafted before the vendor calls.

  • Close the loop from receiving to payment: every delivery matches a purchase order line, every warehouse bin knows its serial numbers, cycle counts are scored against an accuracy gate, and finance three-way matches from the same record, so the question "did we get what we paid for" has one answer instead of three.

  • Ship manufacturing as software before the factory opens: manufacturing bills of materials, engineering change notices, and the drawing tree live in one model, inspection and test plans and first article procedures generate per asset from the design revision, and a failed check opens a nonconformance with the evidence attached and rescores the vendor.

  • Embed with sourcing leads, quality managers, factory operators, and warehouse teams, on their floors and in their vendor calls, and turn their judgment into the systems that decide the order schedule, the cash demand by month, and the payment schedule the company plans against.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've shipped production code in Go, Python, or TypeScript, and you pick up whatever language the problem demands.

  • You've built real features on LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, or open-weight models), MCP servers, and agentic frameworks, and you've put document extraction into production against messy real inputs.

  • You work daily with AI coding tools like Claude Code and Cursor, and you get agents doing useful work autonomously alongside you.

  • You identify problems, design the solution, and ship it without waiting for direction or approval.

  • You've moved fast under deadline while leaving data models and foundations that other engineers extended after you moved on.

  • You've earned credibility with operators in factories, warehouses, or procurement, and driven adoption of your software inside their real deadlines, like a live production run or a quarter-end close.

  • Your product taste shows in what you've shipped: interfaces the floor calls obvious, and workflows that match how the work actually happens.

  • Bonus: MES, ERP, WMS, or TMS systems. BOM lineage, engineering change control, and serialized component traceability. Supplier quality (NCRs, CAPA, FAI). Three-way match and receiving reconciliation. LLM extraction over vendor documents. High-volume hardware supply chains.

Benefits:

  • Competitive total compensation package (cash + equity)

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Retirement plan

  • Generous PTO policy

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Power Generation Team

The Power Generation team designs and builds the power that runs Fluidstack's AI infrastructure, including grids that stand alone with no utility behind them.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Build an islanded grid at gigawatt scale, from a blank sheet. Generation, storage and compute running with no utility behind them, where the machine you design is the only thing holding voltage. No playbook exists at this size, so the architecture you set becomes the reference.

  • Get power online in months, not years. Interconnection queues are measured in years and we do not have them. Generating our own power is how a site goes from signed lease to live compute inside six months, and the power system is the long pole in that plan.

  • Make one power block, then build it a thousand times. A repeatable block and cluster unit, validated once and stamped across the fleet, is the only route to the scale we are targeting. Every bespoke site is schedule we do not get back.

  • Design a grid whose largest load answers back. Compute is not passive demand here. Load behaviour, curtailment and shedding are design variables you negotiate and specify, a lever almost no power system engineer has ever been handed.

Role Scope

  • Design the MV network. Design the medium-voltage network that carries power from each generation block to the data halls, inside the system design basis, as one standard that every site deploys and that grows by adding blocks rather than by redesign.

  • Design the cluster tie and MV substations. Cover bus arrangement, transformer selection, tie and transfer schemes, and the switching sequences that let a new block energize next to live ones without an outage.

  • Run the network studies yourself. Size feeders, cable and transformers to the load and produce the load flow, voltage drop, short circuit, protection coordination, and EMT studies of switching, energization and islanded transients behind them, as models that rerun for each site's layout and block count.

  • Set protection and specifications. Set the protection philosophy and relay settings for an inverter-dominated network with limited fault current, and write the standard specifications for MV switchgear, transformers, cable and relaying that ship with every block.

  • Define the envelope. State the block count, feeder length, fault level and load step the standard holds for, set the triggers that send a site to a site-specific study, and fold what each energized site teaches back into the next revision.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 10+ years of experience in medium-voltage power distribution design, including network studies, protection coordination, and MV switchgear and substation design.

  • You've personally built power system models of an MV network and produced the load flow, short circuit and cable sizing results that went into issued-for-construction drawings.

  • You've built electromagnetic transient (EMT) models of switching, energization or islanded events, such as transformer inrush, ferroresonance or inverter-dominated fault response, and changed a design because of what they showed.

  • You've set the protection philosophy and relay settings for a system with limited or variable fault current, and you can walk through the coordination that proved it.

  • You've designed MV distribution down to the hardware, including metal-clad switchgear, transformers, cable and duct bank ampacity, and grounding, and defended those choices against NEC, NFPA 70E and IEEE requirements with engineers of record and AHJs.

  • You've designed an MV substation or bus tie scheme that let new capacity energize next to live load, and written the switching sequence the operators followed.

  • You've turned a one-off design into a standard that other engineers applied across multiple projects, and written its design basis clearly enough that they could use it without calling you.

  • You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

  • Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

  • Bonus: Transmission-side study and protection work, including interconnection and EMT studies. Grid-forming and islanded systems. A Professional Engineer licence.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

  • Build the team. Hire the rotating equipment engineers who extend the qualification, commissioning and operations work across the fleet.

  • You've written an equipment specification and acceptance test procedure, witnessed factory and site acceptance against it, and rejected or held a unit that did not meet it.

  • You've owned distributed generation in operation, in oil and gas, mining, island utilities, CHP or data centers, tracked heat rate, availability and maintenance cost unit by unit, and changed how the units were run to extend overhaul intervals or cut fuel burn.

  • You've integrated fuel-based generation with inverter-based resources on the same bus or in an islanded system, and you can say exactly what the engine needs from the controller and what the controller needs from the engine.

  • You've commissioned generation through first fire and load testing, and you were on site when a unit tripped on a load step and worked out why.

  • You've worked across more than one generation technology or fuel, and you can explain which of your experience transfers to the next one and which does not.

  • You write clearly enough that an OEM application engineer, a site technician and a CEO each get the decision they need from the same document.

  • You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

  • Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

Alternative and blended fuels (hydrogen blends, methanol, dual-fuel diesel) and electrochemical generation such as solid oxide fuel cells. Condition monitoring, predictive maintenance and emissions controls (SCR, oxidation catalysts) and their interplay with air permits.

  • Get power online in months, not years. Interconnection queues are measured in years and we do not have them. Generating our own power is how a site goes from signed lease to live compute inside six months, and the power system is the long pole in that plan.

  • Design a grid whose largest load answers back. Compute is not passive demand here. Load behaviour, curtailment and shedding are design variables you negotiate and specify, a lever almost no power system engineer has ever been handed.

Role Scope

  • Own the control stack. Own the control stack for fully off-grid campuses: the site energy management system, the plant controller for each power block and the dispatch logic across PV, BESS and gas, as one standard architecture that scales from a single block to a gigawatt-scale campus energized in six months.

  • Write sequences our own code runs. Turn the control philosophy into sequences of operation covering every operating mode, source transition, blackstart path, emergency shed and degraded state, and prove each one in simulation and on a hardware-in-the-loop bench before the plant is energized. Build the plant model library and bench so any controller, vendor or our own, is tested against our plant before it ships to site.

  • Hold the generation side of the control contract. Extend the contract between the power plant and the data center from one plant and one facility to many blocks feeding many buildings, with load reduction deadlines measured in seconds that both sides are measured against in production.

  • Decide what we buy and what we build. Choose which components we bring in to energize the first campuses faster and which we build first, replace each bought piece with our own code on a planned schedule, and hold every supplier to our specification and conformance tests so Fluidstack keeps its configuration, its data and a clean exit.

  • Lead commissioning and tuning in the field. Take each campus through frequency and voltage response, load-step testing against real AI load profiles and every mode transition, and fold each finding back into the standard so the next campus starts tuned.

  • Build the team. Hire the controls software and test engineers who build the stack with you, sequenced against the components we replace first.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 10+ years of experience in plant controls and energy management systems for utility-scale hybrid plants, including sequences of operation, controls software, and field commissioning.

  • You've owned the plant controller or EMS on a utility-scale hybrid plant combining at least two of PV, BESS and thermal generation, and you can name the sites and the megawatts it dispatches today.

  • You've written sequences of operation for source transitions, blackstart or islanding, and you've stood on site when they ran against energized equipment, including the times they did not work.

  • You've shipped control software as a product, version-controlled, tested and released to running plants, and you know what changes when the loop closes on a real turbine or inverter fleet.

  • You've brought a third-party controller or component into a live plant to hit a date, held the vendor to a specification through factory and site acceptance, and later replaced it with your own code without an outage.

  • You've designed an interface between two control systems owned by different parties, with the data, timing and failure behavior written down and tested, not left to whoever integrated it.

  • You've tuned a plant in the field, frequency and voltage response, ramp rates and load steps, and you can explain the tradeoff behind each setting you left in place.

  • You write clearly enough that an OEM controls engineer, a commissioning agent and a CEO each get the decision they need from the same document.

  • You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

  • Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

  • Bonus: Islanded or weak-grid operation (island utilities, mining and remote microgrids, offshore). Real-time simulation and hardware-in-the-loop testing. Industrial control protocols and OT security (DNP3, IEC 61850, IEC 62443).

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

The Data Center Operations Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Operate at the scale of a nation, not a building. Gigawatt-scale infrastructure, growing fast. You won't just run a data center; you'll run infrastructure the size of a G7.

  • Fly the plane while it's being built. Running flawless operations inside a live construction zone, adapting in real time and turning the pace of build-out into our advantage. You will redefine operational excellence.

  • Write the playbook, don't inherit it. Most operators step into someone else's system. Here you build one, leaving your fingerprints on how the whole company runs. As we scale 100x, you'll set the standards, shape the operating model, and grow the team by the thousands.

Role Scope

  • Run the night shift. Work 7 PM to 7 AM, keeping receiving, staging, and parts delivery moving while the site runs around the clock.

  • Operate forklifts, pallet jacks, and other warehouse equipment safely to receive, move, stage, and ship critical infrastructure at high velocity.

  • Load, unload, inspect, and organize incoming hardware, ensuring every shipment is accounted for and ready for deployment.

  • Pick, pack, and deliver parts quickly and accurately so technicians and engineers always have what they need to keep the data center moving.

  • Maintain an organized, clean, and deployment-ready warehouse, keeping inventory accessible and material flowing efficiently across the site.

  • Run inventory counts, stock replenishment, and asset tracking with precision, maintaining accurate inventory and preventing operational delays.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You're available to work nights, 7 PM to 7 AM, on a consistent rotation.

  • You've worked in a warehouse, distribution center, manufacturing environment, construction site, or other hands-on operational setting where safety, speed, and accuracy matter.

  • You're comfortable operating forklifts or are willing to become certified, and you take pride in moving material safely and efficiently.

  • You're dependable, physically active, and enjoy work that keeps you on your feet while solving real operational problems.

  • You stay organized in fast-moving environments, take ownership of your work, and don't wait to be told what needs to get done.

  • You communicate well, work effectively as part of a team, and understand that every shipment, pallet, and part plays a role in keeping critical infrastructure online.

  • Bonus: Experience with warehouse management systems, barcode scanners, shipping and receiving, inventory control, data center hardware, or high-growth operational environments.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

 - Write the playbook, don't inherit it. Most operators step into someone else's system. Here you build one, leaving your fingerprints on how the whole company runs. As we scale 100x, you'll set the standards, shape the operating model, and grow the team by the thousands.

 - Load, unload, inspect, and organize incoming hardware, ensuring every shipment is accounted for and ready for deployment.

 - Pick, pack, and deliver parts quickly and accurately so technicians and engineers always have what they need to keep the data center moving.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Power Generation Team

The Power Generation team designs and builds the power that runs Fluidstack's AI infrastructure, including grids that stand alone with no utility behind them.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Build an islanded grid at gigawatt scale, from a blank sheet. Generation, storage and compute run with no utility behind them, and the machine you design is the only thing holding frequency. No playbook exists at this size, so the architecture you set becomes the reference.

  • Get power online in months, not years. Interconnection queues are measured in years and we do not have them. Generating our own power is how a site goes from signed lease to live compute inside six months, and the power system is the long pole in that plan.

  • Make one power block, then build it a thousand times. A repeatable block and cluster unit, validated once and stamped across the fleet, is the only route to the scale we are targeting. Every bespoke site is schedule we do not get back.

  • Design a grid whose largest load answers back. Compute is not passive demand here. Load behaviour, curtailment and shedding are design variables you negotiate and specify.

Role Scope

  • Own the design basis. Fix voltage levels, topology, grounding, redundancy boundaries and the repeatable block and cluster unit for the islanded grid, with v1 and the site and block single-lines issued inside six months.

  • Treat the block as a product. Hold one standard design across sites, drive out the variation that turns a repeatable build back into bespoke engineering, and freeze the design early enough that procurement and construction never absorb late change.

  • Write the grid code and hold vendors to it. Set the internal grid code every generator, BESS, inverter and transformer must meet, own the conformance evidence that proves compliance before equipment ships, and own the technical content of equipment specifications and bid evaluation, with v0.1 in vendors' hands before the first major RFP.

  • Build the model of record. Produce the first-pass generation, BESS and reserve sizing and the first load flow, short circuit and transient stability results yourself, own the study register and its prioritised roadmap, and accept or reject every vendor and EPC study against it.

  • Set stability, protection and phasing. Define the loss-of-largest-unit contingency, reserve policy and a load shedding scheme with compute as a participating resource, negotiate the load behaviour specification with the compute side, and decide whether the next block can be energised safely at every intermediate build state.

  • Close the loop from the field and build the team. Go to site, fold every commissioning finding and installer workaround into the next revision of the standard, and hire the specialists behind you in sequence: protection and HV substation, studies and EMT, and the operations counterpart who will own dispatch, reserves and switching orders.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 10+ years of experience in power system design and studies for islanded or weak-grid systems, including EMT and load flow modeling, protection, and grid-forming inverter integration.

  • You have delivered a real islanded or very weak-grid power system at 100MW or more, on an island or remote utility, a mining or LNG captive plant, an OEM power systems group, or a specialist islanded-systems practice. A grid-tied microgrid is not the same problem.

  • You build the models with your own hands: deep EMT work alongside RMS, and you have personally produced the load flow, short circuit and stability results that decisions were made on.

  • You have designed around grid-forming inverter control and inverter-dominated protection, where there is little or no synchronous machine underneath you to hide behind.

  • You have owned a system design basis that vendors were held to, and you have rejected a vendor or EPC study that did not meet it. You set standards that OEMs and EPCs comply with on technical authority rather than headcount or a title.

  • You have been in the room when an island went dark, and you were the one who had to explain why.

  • You have designed something that got built many times over. You freeze a design, you say no to the change that would have been a small improvement and a large disruption, and you have watched what a late revision does to a supply chain.

  • You spend time where the work happens, and the standards you write are shaped by what installers and operators actually do rather than what the drawing assumed.

  • You're comfortable with regular travel: expect 25% or more, depending on business needs.

  • Most of our engineering team, stakeholders, and work are based in Austin, TX, and we value working in person. We have a strong preference for Austin and run a hybrid model, but we're open to other locations for the right role and candidate.

  • Bonus: ERCOT market and interconnection dynamics. HV substation design at 230kV and above. Professional Engineer licence. Lean practice applied to design and build, including standard work and design freeze discipline. Load shedding and dispatch schemes that treat flexible load as a participating resource. Utility control room and switching order design.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Power Generation Team

The Power Generation team designs, sources and builds the generation that runs Fluidstack's AI infrastructure.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Put solar, storage and gas in the ground at an install rate no one in the construction market has hit. We are building generation across multiple gigawatt sites at once, on a schedule traditional EPC delivery cannot meet.

  • Secure supply at a scale and timeline the supply chain cannot meet, and reshore it ourselves. Cells, containers, transformers and turbines are all constrained, so we qualify new suppliers and stand up domestic capacity instead of waiting in line.

  • Make solar, gas and storage combine into power steady enough to run AI workloads. A training run does not tolerate a dip, so the hybrid plant has to behave like firm generation even when the resource behind it does not.

  • Clear balancing authority certification, firm load rights, permits and interconnection against long clocks and a shifting policy environment. These approvals sit on the critical path to every gigawatt, so we work them years ahead of the build.

Role Scope

  • Own the storage plant design. Lead the electrical design and sizing of multi-hundred-megawatt storage plants, from single line, protection and grounding through power and energy ratings and augmentation strategy, across several concurrent gigawatt sites.

  • Qualify and dual-source BESS vendors. Choose on technical merit, and run factory witness testing, failure mode review and warranty terms alongside supply chain.

  • Define how the plant dispatches. Specify how storage, solar and on-site generation dispatch together so the plant holds a firm load profile through resource swings and generator trips.

  • Get fire safety approved before equipment lands. Drive NFPA 855 compliance, hazard mitigation analysis and large-scale fire test evidence through the AHJ and the insurer before equipment reaches site.

  • Take each plant through commissioning. Complete capacity and round-trip performance testing and controls integration before the first training load connects.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 10+ years of experience in grid-scale battery energy storage engineering, from plant design and sizing through vendor qualification, fire safety approval, and commissioning.

  • You've taken grid-scale battery storage from single line to energized plant, and you can name the sites and the megawatts.

  • You've sized a storage system against a real duty cycle and lived with the result, including the augmentation call and the places the model turned out to be wrong.

  • You've chosen between BESS vendors on technical grounds, sat through factory witness testing, and pushed back on a datasheet that did not survive scrutiny.

  • You've argued NFPA 855 and hazard mitigation analysis in front of an AHJ or an insurer and got to approval.

  • You've integrated storage controls with generation and load so the combined plant behaves as one machine rather than three.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Supply Chain Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Supply gigawatt-scale compute, the largest build out of compute in history. Qualify and dual-source across every critical equipment category, with lead-time and capacity thresholds tied directly to the forward build pipeline.

  • Make supply chain the reason we build faster than anyone. Our modular build redefines speed in this industry, and it lives or dies on supply chain. Keep procurement permanently off the critical path so schedule compression stays our advantage, not our constraint.

  • Build the most accurate supply chain prediction modelling that exists. Use the frontier of AI to forecast lead times, demand, and disruption with a precision the industry has never had, and turn that foresight into a structural edge.

Role Scope

  • Own multi-year commodity strategies for direct material categories (metals, plastics, electronic components, sub-assemblies, MRO), building should-cost models that hold up against supplier pushback.

  • Lead RFI, RFQ, and RFP processes and e-auction bidding events across global supply markets, qualifying suppliers on capacity, financial health, and risk through structured assessments and site audits.

  • Negotiate and execute Master Supply Agreements, Long-Term Agreements, and pricing amendments, coordinating with Legal and Finance on annual price reviews and cost-down commitments.

  • Run Quarterly Business Reviews and supplier scorecards tracking quality (PPM), delivery (OTD), cost, and responsiveness, and build dual-source and geographic diversification plans to close out single-source risk.

  • Deliver annual cost reduction targets through value engineering, demand aggregation, and supplier consolidation, partnering with Engineering on design-for-cost decisions ahead of new product introductions.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've built and owned multi-year commodity strategies for direct material categories, backed by should-cost models that survive supplier pushback.

  • You've negotiated complex, multi-year supply agreements and pricing amendments across global markets, including Asia-Pacific, Europe, and North America.

  • You've run RFI, RFQ, and RFP processes and e-auction bidding events end to end, from supplier qualification through contract signature.

  • You track supplier performance with scorecards spanning quality (PPM), delivery (OTD), and cost, and you use commodity indices (LME, CBOT) and hedging mechanisms to get ahead of pricing swings instead of reacting to them.

  • You've delivered measurable annual cost reduction through value engineering, demand aggregation, or supplier consolidation, and you can show the numbers behind it.

  • You've worked inside ERP and procurement platforms (SAP, Oracle, Ariba, Coupa, Jaggaer, or equivalent) enough to run sourcing events and spend analytics without hand-holding.

  • Bonus: CPSM, CSCP, or CPP certification. Familiarity with quality systems (PPAP, APQP, IATF 16949, ISO 9001) for supplier qualification. Direct materials sourcing in a hardware or hyperscale infrastructure environment.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

Role Scope

  • Execute the daily cycle count reconciliation for five data center sites and warehouses from the WMS count export, following the documented method step for step: dedupe the scans, net shortages against recorded transactions, and publish each site's variance tracker before the morning deadline, seven days a week on a rotation.

  • Post the WMS corrections each variance calls for (quantity adjustments with reason codes, location transfers, part alias fixes) within the authority limits set by the Program Manager, Inventory Control, and log the site lead's root cause and resolution on every row until it closes.

  • Request same-day recounts and bin checks through the established site contacts, confirm the results land in the system, and verify on the next count that the correction held.

  • Triage every below-minimum and zero-on-hand alert the day it fires against the alert decision tree, enter and maintain min/max values and exception fixes as directed, and escalate anything the rules do not cover to the Program Manager the same day.

  • Prepare the system-pulled, cross-checked inputs for the daily customer count report and the weekly accuracy review, and work the record-integrity backlog (17,000+ serialized assets without a location, duplicate bin records, 3PL discrepancy lists) against the plan and dates the Program Manager sets.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've done cycle counts and variance reconciliation as a daily job in a WMS, and you can show a tracker or log you kept current for months.

  • You work a documented procedure the same way every day, and when a step does not fit the situation you flag it and take action.

  • You find the wrong row with lookups, pivots, dedupe and formula checks, and you've caught your own errors before anyone else saw them.

  • You've posted adjustments and transfers in an inventory system with reason codes, and you know which ones you're allowed to post yourself and which ones need a sign-off.

  • You've asked a warehouse team you don't work beside to recount a bin the same day, and you closed the loop when the result came back.

  • You've kept a seven-day cadence on a rotation, working remotely from the operation you support, and your Sunday output looks the same as your Tuesday output.

  • Bonus: WMS systems (SAP EWM, NetSuite, Manhattan, DCIM platforms). Data center hardware (optics, trays, network switches, GPU servers). Spreadsheet automation or query languages (Apps Script, SQL). Barcode or RFID scanning workflows.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

    • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

      Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The R&D Team

Fluidstack's R&D organization designs the next generations of our data center product: modular builds, new cooling and power architectures, and the lab-to-field pipeline that turns prototypes into deployable capacity. The team spans mechanical, electrical, controls, and compute engineering, working with manufacturing and supply chain to move designs from first article to repeatable production at gigawatt scale.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Running several first-of-a-kind power and cooling pilots at once without letting any of them stall.

  • Keeping every engineering team pointed at the same priorities as the product and the company change quickly.

  • Getting the data in front of leadership fast enough to make technical bets with confidence.

Role Scope

  • Be the right hand to the Head of Development Engineering. Work side by side with the head of R&D, take their highest-priority problems off their plate, and drive each one to a decision or a delivered result.

  • Drive initiatives across the organization. Own cross-team efforts from first scoping to done, and do whatever the work needs, from analysis and vendor calls to schedules and follow-up, so the team moves fast.

  • Coordinate across every engineering team. Work directly with each engineering team and its leader to line up projects, pilots, and R&D efforts so priorities, owners, and dates stay clear.

  • Shape technical direction. Build the first-order analysis leadership needs to set the company's technical direction, and carry decisions back into the teams that execute them.

  • Run the operating rhythm. Own the R&D leadership cadence: agendas, decisions, action items, and status reports that name what is slipping and what it takes to recover.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • 3-7 years of experience in engineering, technical program management, consulting, or operations, ideally around hardware, energy, or infrastructure.

  • An engineering or technical degree, or equivalent hands-on technical depth.

  • You want a steep learning curve and broad exposure to how an R&D organization is run, and you are ready to work hard to get it.

  • You are comfortable in an engineering conversation and build your own first-pass models and analysis.

  • You write clearly and keep senior people informed without being chased.

  • You take on any task the team needs, learn new domains fast, and are open about what you do not know yet.

  • Low ego and self-directed: you manage your own work, manage upward, and keep things moving without being asked.

  • Bonus: Experience at a startup or on a first-of-a-kind project. Exposure to power, cooling, or data center systems.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

Role Scope

  • Negotiate behind-the-meter PPAs, tolling agreements, and heat rate options with generation owners and developers for multi-hundred-megawatt data center campuses.

  • Negotiate gas supply, transport, and basis arrangements that lock in fuel price and deliverability for each behind-the-meter site before the build starts.

  • Diligence prospective behind-the-meter gas sites for pipeline access, fuel constraints, air permitting, and power delivery risk before we commit to a lease.

  • Evaluate generation equipment (for example turbines and reciprocating engines) on heat rate, availability, lead time, emissions, and delivered cost, and turn it into a clear recommendation for leadership.

  • Quarterback development, engineering, legal, and finance from site selection through executed supply contracts to energization, and flag cost and schedule exposure before it reaches leadership.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've personally negotiated behind-the-meter PPAs, tolls, or heat rate options where the economics had to hold through project finance and final deal terms.

  • You've negotiated gas supply agreements and managed fixed-price, index, and basis exposure, and you know which fuel constraints break a plant's dispatch.

  • You've diligenced a gas-fired site from pipeline access and fuel deliverability through air permits and power delivery, and you know what kills a site early.

  • You've compared generation technologies on heat rate, spark-spread economics, and reliability, and your analysis drove an equipment decision.

  • You've built the techno-economic models behind these deals and defended the sensitivities to lenders, investors, or executives.

  • You quarterback across engineering, legal, finance, and operations, and you write clearly enough to distill a technical question into a decision and a next step for a CEO.

  • Bonus: Multi-market power experience (ERCOT, PJM, MISO, WECC). Plant dispatch and fuel optimization (generator, asset manager, or trading desk). Large-load and utility interconnection. Pipeline capacity and midstream contracting.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

Role Scope

  • Diligence prospective sites across both paths to power, grid interconnection and behind-the-meter generation, and turn each one into a go or no-go recommendation in days rather than weeks.

  • Build and own the delivered cost of power model across candidate sites and both paths, from tariffs and network upgrade exposure on the grid side to gas basis, transport, heat rate, and availability behind the meter.

  • Be the single source of truth on where every site stands, queue position and study milestones on the grid side, contracted fuel and generation position behind the meter, and what has to happen next on each.

  • Run the diligence file on every live site, tariff filings and interconnection studies, pipeline and interconnect agreements, air permits, offtake term sheets, and generation specifications, kept clean enough to walk a counterparty or a lender through cold.

  • Support the Leads through live negotiations with term sheet comparisons, sensitivity runs, counterparty and credit screens, and the one number that decides the question, delivered before the next call rather than after it.

  • Track the markets and the policy that set the rules we build under, ISO large load processes, rate cases and tariff changes, and gas fundamentals in the basins we are buying into.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've built a model that someone traded, invested, or committed capital off, and you can defend every assumption in it under pressure.

  • You've read a contract, tariff, or study report closely and pulled out the two or three terms that actually change the economics, rather than summarising the whole thing.

  • You turn a disordered data room into a one page recommendation that names the thing the decision actually turns on.

  • You've caught a material error in someone else's work before it reached a decision maker, and you raised it rather than working around it.

  • You've been dropped into a market or an asset class you did not know and been useful inside a few weeks, and you can point to how you got up to speed.

  • You write up what you found the same day you found it, so a site file never depends on what is in your head.

  • Bonus: Commodities trading or analytics desks in gas or power (basis, storage, transport, fundamentals). Origination and structuring teams, especially PPA and offtake work. Large load or generator interconnection across one or more ISOs (ERCOT, PJM, MISO, SPP, WECC). Transaction diligence from M&A, project finance, or infrastructure investing. Behind-the-meter or distributed generation development. Modelling and data tooling (Python, SQL, ICE and CME data, Wood Mackenzie, Velocity Suite).

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law.   • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Security Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • You're securing the frontier of AI. The model weights training on our infrastructure are the most valuable and most targeted artifacts in technology, and we're standing up the compute to hold them faster than anyone ever has. A breach isn't a leak, it's the frontier walking out the door.

  • Build the entire security program from scratch. Most leaders inherit someone else's system and spend a career patching it. Here you own it end to end, bare metal to boardroom, as we scale across continents.

  • Your threat surface is measured in gigawatts. The customers running on our infrastructure are building the most consequential technology in human history, and being responsible for the physical and logical security of that work makes everything else feel small.

Role Scope

  • Threat model OT systems and environments across the fleet: SCADA platforms, BMS and EPMS, cooling and power systems, and the sensor networks that feed them.

  • Design the architecture and segmentation that keeps a gigawatt-scale OT estate defensible: network zones, remote access paths, and the IT/OT boundary.

  • Forward-deploy with controls engineering to secure operational deployments, from PLC code pipelines and virtualized controllers to the SCADA layer above them.

  • Serve as the security consultant to power, controls, commissioning, and site teams as new capacity energizes, turning review requests into guidance teams can actually deploy.

  • Work with the detection and response org to understand and tune OT-environment detection coverage, and respond alongside incident responders when attacks reach OT infrastructure.

  • Lead engagements with hardware OEM’s on product security requirements and use cases such as firmware security, tamper evidence, and counterfeit detection to address supply chain risk.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You can architect isolation at every layer it exists: hardware, firmware, hypervisor, kernel, container, network fabric, and physical.

  • You understand AI compute infrastructure as a system (accelerators, high-speed interconnects, parallel storage, schedulers) and know where each component breaks a classical security assumption.

  • You've done original work in systems or ML security, published or shipped, and can turn research into architecture that engineers actually build.

  • You defend design decisions in review on their merits, and change them when someone closer to the metal proves you wrong.

  • Bonus: Confidential computing and attestation depth. Weights custody or cryptographic key custody at scale. A publication record in systems or ML security.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • You're securing the frontier of AI. The model weights training on our infrastructure are the most valuable and most targeted artifacts in technology, and we're standing up the compute to hold them faster than anyone ever has. A breach isn't a leak, it's the frontier walking out the door.

  • Build the entire security program from scratch. Most leaders inherit someone else's system and spend a career patching it. Here you own it end to end, bare metal to boardroom, as we scale across continents.

  • Your threat surface is measured in gigawatts. The customers running on our infrastructure are building the most consequential technology in human history, and being responsible for the physical and logical security of that work makes everything else feel small.

Role Scope

  • Own exposure and vulnerability management across the estate: external attack surface, cloud and Kubernetes, corporate endpoints, network infrastructure, and the bare-metal fleet beneath them.

  • Extend exposure and vulnerability management across the corporate fleet (macOS, Windows, Linux): OS and application patch posture, first-party and third-party software, and drift from approved baselines.

  • Cover software outside our managed and approved catalogs: unmanaged apps and SaaS, package-level software on endpoints (npm, PyPI, Homebrew), and browser and IDE extensions. Identify it, assess it, and drive it to remediation or removal.

  • Build the engineering that makes it work: asset inventory, scanner orchestration, deduplication, and prioritization built on reachability and real-world exploitation rather than raw CVSS.

  • Engineer remediation into the workflows teams already use, so findings land as owned tickets, fixes ride existing pipelines, and closure verifies automatically.

  • Remediate alongside the teams that own the systems: write the patch PR, harden the base image, fix the IaC module, and ship the config change rather than just requesting it.

  • Extend the program past where enterprise playbooks run out: BMC and device firmware, GPU drivers, host images at fleet scale, and the long tail of data center equipment.

  • Run intake for pen test findings and external reports, and report exposure honestly: what's reachable, what's exploited in the wild, what's accepted and by whom.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've built vulnerability management as an engineering problem: pipelines, automation, and integrations rather than spreadsheet triage.

  • You write production-quality automation (Python or similar) and have wired scanners, asset systems, and ticketing into something coherent.

  • You've run prioritization that survives contact with reality: KEV, EPSS, reachability, and the judgment to overrule all three.

  • You've fixed vulnerabilities yourself, in someone else's codebase or infrastructure, and your pull requests got merged because they were good, not because security demanded it.

  • You've driven remediation at scale through teams that don't report to you and kept SLAs credible without burning the relationships.

  • You can take a technology class most programs never touch, firmware or GPU stacks or data center equipment, and stand up a defensible assessment approach instead of waiting for a vendor to sell you one.

  • You've run vulnerability and exposure coverage on corporate endpoints and third-party software, including the unmanaged long tail of shadow apps, packages, and extensions.

  • Bonus: External attack surface management platforms. Firmware or BMC security depth. CSPM/KSPM tooling. Exploit development or reachability validation. Endpoint management and patching tooling (MDM, EDR), software inventory, and extension and supply chain risk.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE SECURITY TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - You're securing the frontier of AI. The model weights training on our infrastructure are the most valuable and most targeted artifacts in technology, and we're standing up the compute to hold them faster than anyone ever has. A breach isn't a leak, it's the frontier walking out the door.

 - Build the entire security program from scratch. Most leaders inherit someone else's system and spend a career patching it. Here you own it end to end, bare metal to boardroom, as we scale across continents.

 - Your threat surface is measured in gigawatts. The customers running on our infrastructure are building the most consequential technology in human history, and being responsible for the physical and logical security of that work makes everything else feel small.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Stand up FluidStack's insider risk and counterintelligence program from zero: operating model, roadmap, and the controls that protect some of the most targeted compute infrastructure in the world.

 - Design and land technical controls by working through the rest of the security org: detection engineering for monitoring and analytics, IT and infrastructure for identity and data controls, physical security for the badge-to-bare-metal seam.

 - Run insider risk incidents end to end with legal and HR, from first signal through resolution.

 - Write the program's policy library and carry it through legal, HR, and leadership to adoption.

 - Own the program's stakeholder relationships: align with legal and HR on process, and keep the program legible and credible to the workforce it protects.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c.

 - You've built or rebuilt an insider risk program in a commercial environment before, more than once, and you know which parts of the playbook survive contact with a private-sector workforce.

 - You came up through the intelligence community or an adjacent national security mission, and you've already made the translation of counterintelligence tradecraft into corporate practice.

 - You've shipped technical controls by working through teams that don't report to you: detection, identity, IT, physical security.

 - You've written monitoring and investigations policy that got adopted, surviving scrutiny from legal and HR rather than sitting on a shelf.

 - You work fluently with legal and HR, and can take a sensitive incident to each of them in their own language.



We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

AI Screening Notice https://fluidstack.io/legal/ai-screening-notice
Ashby Bias Audit https://fluidstack.io/legal/ashby-bias-audit
