jobs.title: Structural Engineer, R&D
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Civil, Structural and Architectural R&D Team

The CSA R&D team designs the template buildings, foundations, and modular structures that Fluidstack builds again and again for gigawatt-scale AI data centers. We engineer the design once, prove it, and hand delivery teams a package they can build without reinventing it.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Design a repeatable building and foundation system that survives fabrication, transport, and site conditions across very different geographies.

  • Bring structural engineering in-house so design decisions close in days, not in weeks of waiting on an outside engineer of record.

  • Resolve the collisions between structure, equipment, and MEP: load paths, penetrations, attachment points, and tolerances in a tight envelope.

  • Turn factory and field lessons into engineered fixes in the next design revision.

Role Scope

  • Own the structural calculations. Run gravity, lateral, foundation, lifting, and transport analyses for template buildings, equipment supports, skids, and modular structures, and stand behind the numbers.

  • Produce the detailed designs. Take structural systems from concept through fabrication-ready drawings, connection details, and specifications without handing the work to a third party.

  • Make the design repeatable. Build the standard details, load tables, and design rules that let the same structure be built at many sites with minimal site-specific engineering.

  • Integrate across disciplines. Resolve where structure meets architecture, mechanical, electrical, and fire protection so the package builds clean.

  • Run structural support for the factory and the field. Answer RFIs, review shop drawings and submittals, and engineer fixes into the next revision.

  • Hand off to delivery. Package the design so site teams, fabricators, and local engineers of record can execute it with minimal rework.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You have 7+ years of structural engineering on industrial, mission-critical, or data center buildings, with steel, concrete, and foundation design in your own hands.

  • You perform your own calculations and produce your own detailed designs. You do not need an outside engineer to close a design.

  • You know the codes cold: IBC, ASCE 7, AISC 360, ACI 318, and how to apply them across seismic, wind, and snow regions.

  • You work in structural analysis and drafting tools daily (RISA, SAP2000, ETABS, RAM, Revit, or equivalent) and your drawings build without a stream of fabricator calls.

  • You have designed pre-engineered metal buildings, equipment foundations, or modular and transported structures, and you treat lifting and transport loads as first-class constraints.

  • You work across disciplines instead of throwing problems over walls, and you iterate fast without losing configuration control.

  • Bonus: PE license (SE a plus). Experience as engineer of record on hyperscale data center or industrial projects. DfMA and modular construction depth.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.


Applicant Privacy Notice
AI Screening Notice
Ashby Bias Audit

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Construction Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Put gigawatts in the ground, faster than anyone has. We're delivering one of the largest data center buildouts of its kind, with many sites running at once. Traditional construction management breaks at this scale, so we're building the model that replaces it.

  • Throw out traditional construction and invent how gigawatts get built. Tons of tools, layers of process, and administrative drag don't get you there. You'll strip all of that out and win by solving the real problem and beating the goal, not by managing toward it.

  • Productize the data center so we can build it a thousand times. You'll turn one-off construction into a repeatable, modular build, where the hundredth site goes up faster and cleaner than the first. That repeatability is the only way to reach the scale we're targeting.

Role Scope

  • Run technical due diligence on every site from Site Acquisitions' handoff to break ground, directing environmental and civil engineers through environmental site assessments, land and boundary surveys, and traffic impact studies.

  • Make the go or no-go call on dirt: buildable, on time, on budget, with no deal-killers or permanent risks before we transact.

  • Negotiate and organize contracts directly, joining risk-profile decisions and taking big commercials off leadership's plate.

  • Bring on the civil engineer, architect, and GC, and own the master budget, milestone schedule, and floor access dates across five or more sites at once.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've personally run technical due diligence on land and can walk site identification to break ground in order, from the first environmental assessments and land surveys on, saying what you did yourself at each step.

  • You've directed environmental and civil engineers and read traffic impact studies closely enough to challenge them.

  • You've decided what kills a deal and what is acceptable risk, and told leadership a site was clean enough to transact.

  • You've negotiated or organized contracts yourself.

  • You run several projects at once on your own and bring leadership a decision.

  • Bonus: Owner-side land development (greenfield industrial, commercial, energy). Hyperscale data center development or pre-construction. Utility and mineral rights diligence (water, power, interconnection). Modular or prefabricated delivery.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Development Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Find enough land to deploy multiple gigawatts a week. By 2030 we need to bring on multiple gigawatts of new capacity every week, which means securing sites at a pace and scale no one in the industry has operated at. You'll own finding and locking that land ahead of the build.

  • Get power online in months, not years. Most of the clock runs before the lease is ever signed. You'll optimize the pre-signature work, site diligence, permitting, and development, so a site goes from signed lease to live power in under six months.

  • Acquire 10s to 100s of GWs behind the meter. Reaching that scale means generating on-site instead of waiting on grid interconnection. You'll secure the land and behind-the-meter solar generation to get there.

Role Scope

Manage the team and scale the program responsible for sourcing multiple GWs of US powered land, powered shell, and turnkey opportunities through a network of brokers, landowners, and developers you build.

  1. Run diligence on every candidate site: utility and behind-the-meter power at 4200MW+ scale, with security, availability, and ramp validated directly with utilities; buildability from title, surveys, geotechnical, and environmental reports; and permitting requirements mapped against our construction schedule.

  2. Negotiate leases, PSAs, and JV structures with landowners, developers, data center operators, and private equity firms, and test each deal's financeability and multi-year cost with Finance and executive leadership.

  3. Direct vendor due diligence, including on-site audits with specialist engineers, and work with the DC Design team so every site meets our current technical requirements for scale and design.

  4. Own capacity planning and forecasting across all clients and regions so capacity is ready for new and unforeseen projects, and build and mentor the site selection team as it scales.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've led hyperscale data center site acquisitions from first look to signature, and you personally negotiated the powered land and site development deals you closed.

  • You've closed large, multi-party real estate deals across leases, PSAs, and JVs while running a multi-site portfolio at the same time.

  • You've walked away from sites that looked good on paper because the title, geotechnical report, permitting path, or utility study said otherwise.

  • Brokers, landowners, and developers bring you sites before they reach the market, because you built those relationships and kept them.

  • You've built site selection processes and systems that held up as deal volume and team size grew quickly.

  • You bring executive leadership, finance, design, and construction to a site decision with a clear recommendation and the reasoning behind it.

  • You're on site when it matters, with travel of 20% or more.

  • Experience with behind-the-meter and bridge-to-utility power solutions,JV structuring and project finance, and large-load interconnection and utility tariff processes.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Security Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • You're securing the frontier of AI. The model weights training on our infrastructure are the most valuable and most targeted artifacts in technology, and we're standing up the compute to hold them faster than anyone ever has. A breach isn't a leak, it's the frontier walking out the door.

  • Build the entire security program from scratch. Most leaders inherit someone else's system and spend a career patching it. Here you own it end to end, bare metal to boardroom, as we scale across continents.

  • The industry's playbook was written for one building at a time. Vendor-managed appliances, manual process, and standards that assume a security team walks the floor. None of that survives contact with what we're building, so we build what should exist rather than buying what does.

  • Your threat surface is measured in gigawatts. The customers running on our infrastructure are building the most consequential technology in human history, and being responsible for the physical and logical security of that work makes everything else feel small.

Role Scope

  • Keep the systems online. Keep the campus's cameras, readers, door controllers, intercoms, and the head-end servers, storage and switches behind them online and reporting. Find the root cause of each failure before replacing hardware.

  • Repair on-site infrastructure. Troubleshoot and repair cable runs, failed drives, power supplies, DIMMs, NICs and optics, degraded RAID sets, and hosts that fail to boot. Keep the as-builts and device inventory current.

  • Accept new builds. Accept new data centers and expansions from the delivery team: walk down their work and the integrator's against the acceptance criteria before it enters support. Help with commissioning when the schedule requires it.

  • Work the remediation queue. Work the on-site remediation queue to the response targets in the support agreement: device swaps, firmware updates, resets, and the service requests that used to be integrator truck rolls. Escort and verify outside technicians when they are needed.

  • Keep site hardware working. Keep the hardware the guard force, GSOC and site operations use working: badge printers, visitor kiosks, turnstiles and vehicle gates.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You have maintained security devices at data center scale: cameras, readers, controllers and intercoms.

  • You terminate, test and certify copper and fiber cabling, and your labels, as-builts and inventory match what is installed.

  • You have worked hands-on in a live data center or another critical facility, fix local issues on your own, and know which changes to flag before making them.

  • You read drawings and punch lists, can tell finished integrator work from unfinished, and hold contractors to the spec.

  • You troubleshoot from the device up through the switch: PoE, link, port and VLAN config, DHCP.

  • You administer Linux and Windows hosts: imaging, patching, drive replacement, and recovering a host after a failed reboot.

  • You have taken over work from an integrator, including documenting what they did not.

  • Bonus: Enterprise video management and access control platforms. IP camera and access controller hardware. Network fundamentals for device fleets (PoE budgets, VLANs, 802.1X). Server and storage hardware and Linux container basics. Manufacturer and BICSI certifications.

Physical Requirements

  • Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

  • Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

  • Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

  • Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

  • Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

Role Scope

  • Build the capability. Build Fluidstack's protective intelligence and investigations capability from the ground up; set analytic standards, quality expectations, and case management discipline that hold as the program scales with the company's footprint across multiple continents, with room to grow it into a team.

  • Own the program. Own the end-to-end protective intelligence program: threat intake and triage, monitoring, open-source research, case management, reporting, and dissemination to executives, security leadership, and operational teams.

  • Mature investigations. Build and mature investigative capabilities by partnering with HR, insider threat, and cybersecurity to implement risk-based background processes and continuous monitoring aligned with Fluidstack's scaling pace.

  • Assess threats. Conduct threat assessments and investigations on potentially threatening communications, indicators from open sources, and commercial databases; apply structured analytic techniques to prioritize risks and recommend actions.

  • Run lean. Establish a lean investigative framework that leverages other departments and tools across the security organization and the wider enterprise.

  • Embed intelligence in operations. Integrate protective intelligence into company processes: hiring and onboarding decisions, visitor and vendor management, executive travel, events, and crisis response, so operations move at full speed without security gaps.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've built and scaled a protective intelligence program or investigations function from early stage, setting the standards and processes that held as the organization grew.

  • You conduct open-source research and threat assessment with rigor: you know how to find signal in noise across social media, commercial databases, and public records, and you know what doesn't constitute a real threat.

  • You've worked in high-threat or high-visibility environments where the stakes on accuracy and judgment were real. You understand when to escalate and when to de-escalate, and stakeholders trust your assessment.

  • You write and brief clearly enough to give a CEO or a security leadership team a decision and a next step from complex, ambiguous information.

  • You partner effectively across functions. You've worked with Legal, HR, Compliance, and Law Enforcement on overlapping concerns without losing sight of what protective intelligence uniquely answers.

  • You've built tooling for people who aren't engineers, and they actually use it instead of working around it.

Role Scope

  • Design the security control plane end to end and make the architecture decisions the rest of the platform locks against, before the first campus depends on them.

  • Build and operate that control plane at every site, on premises where resilience and bandwidth demand it, with a thin management layer in the cloud where that serves better.

  • Own PKI, certificate lifecycle, identity integration, and automated deprovisioning, so access ends the moment employment does rather than at the next audit.

  • Build the integrations, APIs, and monitoring that tell you a site is degrading before anyone files a ticket, on an estate adding campuses faster than any manual model can track.

  • Reject the hand-built, appliance-per-site, vendor-managed pattern the physical security industry treats as normal, and replace it with infrastructure that is versioned, reproducible, and recoverable.

  • Own backup, disaster recovery, and the non-production environment where changes are proven before they reach a live site.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've designed and run a production virtualization and clustered storage platform, and you can walk through a failover you actually tested rather than one you assumed would work.

  • You've been the design authority on an architecture other people built against, and you can name a decision you got wrong and what it cost to unwind.

  • You've owned database high availability and recovery, and you've restored from your own backups rather than trusting that they ran.

  • You run PKI and certificate lifecycle as automation, so expiry is a solved problem rather than something that pages you at 2am.

  • You've integrated identity systems so provisioning and deprovisioning happen without a human in the loop.

  • You've replaced a vendor-managed or hand-built system with something reproducible, and you can explain what the accepted approach gets wrong and why.

  • You write code and scripts as a normal part of the job, not as an occasional exception.

  • Bonus: Video management and access control platforms (Genetec Security Center, Milestone, Lenel). Enterprise virtualization and clustered storage (Hyper-V, VMware vSphere, Nutanix, failover clustering). Database high availability (SQL Server Always On, clustering). Cloud management planes (AWS). Infrastructure as code (Terraform, Ansible, PowerShell DSC).

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.
